Choosing a smartphone brand is a household product choice. Crossing a €500 price tag does not turn that individual purchase into macroeconomics; price size does not rewrite scope.

So the statement is False.

Venture capital may be discussed nationally, but studying one robotics firm's hiring plan keeps the unit at a single business. A national funding backdrop does not reclassify that firm-level study as macro.

So the statement is False.

Summing all startup investment in the country to assess growth moves from one firm to an economy-wide total. That aggregated investment analysis is macroeconomic.

So the statement is True.

Microeconomics explains and predicts how individual businesses and markets behave. One firm's hiring plan is exactly that kind of unit-level target.

So the statement is True.

Startups and small entrepreneurial firms are standard microeconomic units. Economics does not exclude them for being small; scarcity and choice still apply.

So the statement is False.

title: Budget airline seat sale
context: Consider a budget airline cuts base fares on one holiday route and tracks bookings for that route only. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Route-level fare and booking analysis for one airline is microeconomics.
Any airfare change is macroeconomics because airlines operate internationally.
Economics predicts how passengers on that route respond to the fare cut under limited budgets.
If the statistics office later reported national transport inflation, that would be macroeconomics.
Household holiday booking under a fare sale is micro consumption choice.
tactical_explanations:
Fare and booking analysis for one airline on one holiday route is a single-firm, single-market demand study. That is microeconomics.

So the statement is True.

Airlines may fly internationally, but that does not make every route fare decision macro. Scope follows the unit analysed, not the mere fact of cross-border operations.

So the statement is False.

Economics predicts how passengers on that route respond to a fare cut when their holiday budgets are limited. That behavioural response is microeconomic analysis.

So the statement is True.

National transport inflation reported by the statistics office is a general price-level aggregate for the sector. That index move is macroeconomic.

So the statement is True.

One household booking a holiday under a fare sale is allocating a limited travel budget. That consumption choice is microeconomics.

So the statement is True.

title: Tax-funded lighthouse
context: A coastal town funds a lighthouse through general taxation rather than individual tolls. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Money's store-of-value function is strengthened when inflation is very high and unpredictable.
Free riders would benefit from the beam without paying if funding relied purely on voluntary donations.
Tax financing can overcome free-rider problems by compelling contributions from beneficiaries broadly.
Because ships are private businesses, lighthouse services cannot be public goods by definition.
Public goods must always be provided free with zero cost to any taxpayer.
tactical_explanations:
Money stores value only when what a euro buys stays reasonably stable. Very high and unpredictable inflation eats that real value quickly, so the store-of-value function weakens rather than strengthens. The claim has the effect backwards.

So the statement is False.

A lighthouse beam is hard to withhold from ships that did not donate. If funding rested only on voluntary gifts, non-payers would still navigate by the light. That is the free-rider problem in plain form.

So the statement is True.

General taxation gathers contributions from the wider community that benefits from safer navigation. Compulsory payment closes the gap voluntary funding leaves open, so tax finance can overcome free riding for this kind of shared service.

So the statement is True.

Public goods are defined by non-excludability and non-rivalry in use, not by whether the users are private firms. Ships can be private businesses and still rely on a classic public good. User type does not rewrite the category.

So the statement is False.

Public goods are often tax-funded, but that does not make them costless. Society still pays through taxes and forgone alternatives. "Free at the point of use" is not the same as "zero cost to any taxpayer."

So the statement is False.

title: Saving euros under low inflation
context: A worker holds 1,000 euros in a current account while inflation runs slightly below 2%. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Money still stores value but slowly loses some purchasing power under positive inflation.
Slightly below 2% inflation means purchasing power rises every year for cash holders.
Store-of-value function is weaker when inflation is positive even if moderate.
ECB target near 2% contrasts with destabilising very high inflation rates.
Purchasing power of held cash depends on general price level changes domestically.
tactical_explanations:
With inflation slightly below 2%, the nominal 1,000 euros still sits in the account, yet each euro buys a little less over time. Money continues to store value, but positive inflation slowly erodes purchasing power.

So the statement is True.

Positive inflation, even when low, means the general price level is rising. Cash holders therefore lose purchasing power gradually; they do not gain it. "Slightly below 2%" is still inflation, not deflation.

So the statement is False.

Store of value is about keeping real buying power into the future. When inflation is positive, uninvested cash loses some of that power even if the rate is moderate. The function still works, but it works more weakly than under zero inflation.

So the statement is True.

A low, stable target near 2% is meant to keep prices predictable. That setting is far from the chaos of very high inflation that wrecks planning and contracts. The contrast in the claim is economically sound.

So the statement is True.

What held euros buy at home depends on domestic prices. If grocery and rent prices rise, the same balance stretches less far, regardless of other markets. Purchasing power of cash is tied to the local price level.

So the statement is True.

title: Circular flow basics
context: Analyze the circular flow of income and spending: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Stored cash never loses purchasing power because nominal euro amounts stay unchanged on the note.
A banknote's face value freezes its real purchasing power for decades.
Households can only appear on the spending side and never supply labour or capital to firms.
The circular flow shows how income earned from production returns as spending on output.
Government, banks, and foreign trade never appear in any circular-flow diagram.
tactical_explanations:
The printed number on a note can stay fixed while prices rise. Real purchasing power is what goods that cash can buy, so inflation can shrink it even when the nominal amount never changes. "Stored cash never loses purchasing power" is too strong.

So the statement is False.

Face value is a nominal figure. Over decades of rising prices, the same banknote typically buys fewer goods. Real purchasing power is not frozen by the digits on the paper.

So the statement is False.

In the circular flow, households supply labour and capital to firms and receive income in return. They also spend on goods and services. Confining households to the spending side alone erases half of the basic model.

So the statement is False.

Production generates factor incomes for households; households then spend on the goods and services firms produce. That loop of income returning as spending is exactly what the circular-flow idea captures.

So the statement is True.

Simple textbook sketches start with households and firms, but extended diagrams routinely add government, banks, and foreign trade. Saying those actors never appear is incorrect.

So the statement is False.

title: Hyperinflation pocket money
context: In a country with very rapid price rises, a child's 20-euro note buys far less candy monthly. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Very rapid inflation sharply erodes purchasing power of nominally unchanged cash amounts.
Paying with a mobile transfer is exchange using money as medium of exchange.
Store-of-value function of money fails when inflation outpaces ability to spend or invest quickly.
ECB's slightly-below-2% target aims at stability far from such hyperinflation scenarios.
Purchasing power erosion under inflation affects households as well as firms holding cash.
tactical_explanations:
When prices surge month after month, a fixed 20-euro note buys fewer sweets even though the face amount is unchanged. Rapid inflation cuts real purchasing power of nominal cash sharply.

So the statement is True.

A mobile transfer settles a purchase with money balances rather than a direct swap of goods. That is money acting as a medium of exchange, just as a cash handover would.

So the statement is True.

Store of value means holding money for later use without watching its real worth collapse. When inflation races ahead of any chance to spend or reinvest, cash fails at that job. Hyperinflation is the textbook case.

So the statement is True.

The ECB's aim of inflation slightly below 2% is a price-stability target. It sits nowhere near the extreme instability of hyperinflation. The contrast in the claim holds.

So the statement is True.

Anyone holding cash, household or firm, sees real balances shrink when the price level jumps. Purchasing-power erosion under inflation is not limited to one sector.

So the statement is True.

title: National park entry debate
context: Policals debate funding a national park via general tax versus gate fees only. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Clean air and preserved landscape benefits may extend beyond paying visitors, suggesting public-good elements.
Pure gate fees may exclude low-income residents while still leaving non-visitors benefiting from ecosystem services.
Tax funding can address free-rider issues when many benefit without direct payment.
National parks are never public goods because trees are physical objects you can touch.
Free-rider problems occur only in foreign trade and never in domestic environmental policy.
tactical_explanations:
Clean air and landscape quality can spill beyond those who buy a ticket. When benefits are widely shared and hard to fence off, the park has public-good elements even if gate fees exist for entry.

So the statement is True.

Gate fees can shut out low-income visitors while people who never enter may still enjoy cleaner air or biodiversity. Exclusive pricing neither captures every benefit nor settles equity concerns.

So the statement is True.

When many enjoy ecosystem services without paying at the gate, voluntary funding underprovides upkeep. Tax finance spreads the cost across beneficiaries and can ease that free-rider shortfall.

So the statement is True.

Whether something is a public good turns on excludability and rivalry, not on whether you can touch trees. Physical objects can still deliver non-excludable shared benefits. Tangibility alone does not settle the definition.

So the statement is False.

Free-rider logic applies whenever people can enjoy a shared benefit without contributing, including domestic environmental policy. It is not confined to foreign trade.

So the statement is False.

title: Money's three functions
context: Analyze the three functions of money in a modern economy: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: High, erratic inflation makes cash a safer long-term store of value.
Inflation means any one product got dearer in a single aisle.
Street lighting never faces free riders because neighbours always chip in voluntarily.
Because money stores value, its purchasing power never changes over time.
Barter requires a double coincidence of wants, which money helps overcome as medium of exchange.
tactical_explanations:
A long-term store of value needs reasonably stable purchasing power. High, erratic inflation does the opposite: it eats cash balances. Calling that environment "safer" for storing value reverses the lesson.

So the statement is False.

Inflation is a rise in the general price level, not the story of one product becoming dearer in a single aisle. One shelf price can move for many reasons without counting as inflation.

So the statement is False.

Street lighting is hard to exclude from neighbours who refuse to chip in. Voluntary funding invites free riding; neighbours do not "always" pay. The absolute claim fails.

So the statement is False.

Money can store value, but inflation can still change what a stored euro buys. The store-of-value function does not freeze purchasing power forever.

So the statement is False.

Barter works only when each party wants what the other offers at the same time. Money as a medium of exchange breaks that double coincidence by letting people sell for cash and buy elsewhere later.

So the statement is True.

title: Circular flow with government
context: Evaluate government's role in an extended circular flow: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Government collects taxes from households and firms and spends on public services and transfers.
Government spending and taxation appear in extended circular-flow models linking public sector to private actors.
Households never receive anything from government, so no return flow exists in the circular model.
Subsidies and transfers are channels through which government redistributes income in the flow.
The circular flow shows only barter with no role for money as medium of exchange.
tactical_explanations:
In an extended circular flow, government takes taxes from households and firms and channels spending into public services and transfers. That two-way link is standard in the model.

So the statement is True.

Fuller circular-flow diagrams place the public sector between private actors through tax withdrawals and spending injections. Government is not left off the map in those versions.

So the statement is True.

Households often receive transfers, public services, and sometimes public-sector wages. Saying they never get anything back from government erases those return flows.

So the statement is False.

Subsidies and transfers shift purchasing power among households and firms by design. They are the channels through which government redistributes within the flow.

So the statement is True.

Modern circular-flow thinking assumes monetary payments for goods, factors, taxes, and transfers. It is not a barter-only sketch with no medium of exchange.

So the statement is False.

title: Call centre task split
context: A support centre separates billing queries from technical troubleshooting across two teams. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Division of labour by query type lets agents specialise and often resolve cases faster.
Specialisation can reduce training time per agent for their assigned task category.
Households supply factors to firms and receive income that returns as spending in the circular flow.
If the billing team is understaffed, technical agents cannot cover without cross-training gaps.
Dependency between teams can create bottlenecks when one queue overflows.
tactical_explanations:
Splitting billing from technical work lets each team deepen routines for one query type. Specialisation of that kind usually speeds resolution on familiar cases.

So the statement is True.

Agents trained only on billing, or only on troubleshooting, cover a narrower skill set. Onboarding can therefore be shorter than training everyone for every call type.

So the statement is True.

Households supply labour and capital, earn income, and spend on firms' output. That income-spending loop is the core circular flow, and the claim states it correctly.

So the statement is True.

Without cross-training, technical staff lack billing scripts and access. An understaffed billing queue then cannot be covered cleanly, so the staffing claim fits specialisation's downside.

So the statement is True.

When teams depend on each other, overload in one queue spills into the other. That bottleneck risk is the interdependence that comes with divided tasks.

So the statement is True.

title: Subsidy for rail commuters
context: Government pays a per-trip subsidy lowering commuter rail tickets. Evaluate transfers and subsidies:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Barter partners always want exactly the same items, so matching wants is automatic.
Call centres cannot specialise; only factory workers may divide tasks.
Subsidies are identical to public goods because both always require taxation.
Subsidised tickets can shift commuter choices toward rail without making rail a pure public good.
Transfers redistribute resources and can target policy goals such as mobility or environmental aims.
tactical_explanations:
Barter needs a double coincidence of wants: each side must desire what the other offers. That match is not automatic, which is why barter is cumbersome.

So the statement is False.

Division of labour appears in services as well as factories. Call centres routinely split query types across specialised teams. The "only factory workers" limit is wrong.

So the statement is False.

Subsidies support particular goods or groups; public goods are defined by non-excludability and shared consumption. Taxation can fund either, but that does not make the two identical.

So the statement is False.

A fare subsidy can nudge travellers onto rail while seats remain rival and tickets remain excludable. Price support changes incentives; it does not turn rail into a pure public good.

So the statement is True.

Transfers move resources toward chosen groups or aims, including mobility and environmental goals. That redistributive and policy role is exactly what transfers do.

So the statement is True.

title: Export subsidy debate
context: Government considers export subsidies for dairy cooperatives. Evaluate subsidies versus public goods:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Export subsidies transfer public funds to support a specific industry or activity.
Subsidies differ from pure public goods because subsidised goods remain excludable and rival in consumption.
All government spending is automatically a public good regardless of what is funded.
Subsidies can alter producer incentives and prices without making the product non-excludable.
Tax revenue funding subsidies links government to firms in the circular flow.
tactical_explanations:
An export subsidy channels public money toward a named industry or activity, here dairy cooperatives. That targeted fiscal support is what a subsidy is.

So the statement is True.

Subsidised cheese or milk still goes to paying buyers and is used up by those who consume it. Rivalry and excludability remain, unlike classic pure public goods such as defence or street lighting.

So the statement is True.

Government spending covers many things: transfers, subsidies, private-type purchases, and public goods. Funding source alone does not make every outlay a public good.

So the statement is False.

A subsidy can raise producer receipts or lower buyer prices and still leave the product sellable only to those who pay. Incentives shift; excludability need not vanish.

So the statement is True.

Taxes withdraw income from the private sector; subsidy payments inject funds to firms. That tax-and-spend link is how government connects to producers in the circular flow.

So the statement is True.

title: Barter weekend market
context: A hobby market allows only direct swaps: honey for bread, bread for pottery. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Barter requires double coincidence of wants between each pair of traders.
Absence of money as medium of exchange makes multilateral trading chains harder to arrange.
Such swaps still constitute exchange under otherwise unchanged conditions.
Barter eliminates all comparison problems because traders always value goods equally.
Introducing money would add medium of exchange simplifying trades that barter complicates.
tactical_explanations:
Each direct swap works only if both traders want each other's goods at the same moment. That mutual alignment is the double coincidence of wants.

So the statement is True.

Without money, a honey seller who wants pottery may need a chain of intermediate swaps. Arranging those multilateral matches is far harder than a cash sale.

So the statement is True.

Honey for bread is still exchange: each party gives up something to obtain something preferred. Absence of euros does not erase the trade.

So the statement is True.

Barter leaves traders without a shared unit for quoting values, so comparing unlike goods is often harder, not automatic equality of valuation. The claim overstates barter's simplicity.

So the statement is False.

Money as a medium of exchange lets each person sell for cash and buy later from someone else. That removes much of the matching friction barter creates.

So the statement is True.

title: Purchasing power over decades
context: A pensioner notes the same nominal 100 euros buys fewer groceries than thirty years ago. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Only foreign trade creates free-rider problems; domestic public services never do.
Nominal euro amounts automatically preserve real purchasing power regardless of price changes.
Money's store-of-value function is weakened when inflation is positive over long periods.
Inflation slightly below 2% is the ECB's stability target, not a mandate for ever-rising prices without limit.
Purchasing power depends only on foreign exchange rates and never on domestic price levels.
tactical_explanations:
Free-rider problems show up wherever shared benefits are hard to exclude, including domestic parks, lighting, and other public services. Foreign trade is not the only setting.

So the statement is False.

Nominal balances can sit unchanged while prices rise. Real purchasing power then falls. Automatic preservation of real value does not follow from a fixed euro face amount.

So the statement is False.

Positive inflation over long stretches means cash held idle buys less. That erosion weakens money's performance as a store of value, which matches the pensioner's grocery observation.

So the statement is True.

The ECB's price-stability aim is inflation slightly below 2%, a low stable rate, not an instruction to let prices race without limit. The claim states that distinction correctly.

So the statement is True.

Domestic purchasing power of euro cash turns first on domestic prices. Exchange rates matter for foreign goods, but they do not alone determine what groceries cost at home.

So the statement is False.

title: Inflation and purchasing power
context: Review inflation, purchasing power, and price stability: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Barter requires no matching of wants because any trade partners automatically desire identical goods.
Inflation increases purchasing power because prices and money value always move together upward.
Money as a unit of account disappears the moment two currencies exist in tourism.
If prices rise faster than incomes, households can buy fewer goods with the same nominal cash.
Inflation affects only foreign trade and never domestic purchasing power of euro cash.
tactical_explanations:
Barter requires a double coincidence of wants. Partners do not automatically desire identical goods; matching those wants is the hard part.

So the statement is False.

Inflation raises the general price level, so each euro typically buys less, not more. Purchasing power falls when prices climb; it does not rise in lockstep with "money value upward."

So the statement is False.

A unit of account is a common measuring stick for prices and debts. Tourists may see two currencies, yet each still quotes prices in its own unit. Multiple currencies do not erase the function.

So the statement is False.

If prices outpace incomes, the same nominal cash covers a smaller basket. Real consumption capacity shrinks even though the face amounts look unchanged.

So the statement is True.

Domestic inflation directly cuts what euro cash buys at home. The effect is not limited to foreign trade.

So the statement is False.

title: Voluntary donation park cleanup
context: A river park cleanup relies on voluntary donations; many residents enjoy cleaner paths without donating. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Residents who enjoy cleaner paths without paying illustrate the free-rider problem.
Public-good-like benefits may be underprovided when funding depends on voluntary contributions alone.
Tax financing could reduce free riding by requiring contributions from beneficiaries broadly.
Free riders exist only when money functions as medium of exchange and never with public services.
Voluntary funding always delivers optimal public-good levels without any shortfall.
tactical_explanations:
Residents who walk cleaner paths without donating enjoy a benefit others fund. That pattern is the free-rider problem.

So the statement is True.

When enjoyment is shared and payment is voluntary, many hold back and hope others pay. Shared cleanup then tends to be underfunded relative to what the community would collectively prefer.

So the statement is True.

Tax finance requires broader contribution from those who benefit, including people who would otherwise free ride. Compulsory funding can close the voluntary shortfall.

So the statement is True.

Free riding is about enjoying a shared benefit without paying. It arises with public services whether or not money is also used as a medium of exchange elsewhere.

So the statement is False.

Voluntary donation schemes often fall short of the socially preferred level of a shared good. "Always optimal" is too strong.

So the statement is False.

title: Medium of exchange everyday
context: Shoppers pay euros for bread instead of trading socks directly with the baker. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Using euros avoids barter's double coincidence of wants between bread and socks.
Money as medium of exchange separates the act of selling from the act of buying.
Street lighting financed by local tax can address free-rider problems of voluntary funding.
Medium of exchange is one of money's three core functions alongside unit of account and store of value.
Without medium of exchange, every purchase would require direct matching of wants.
tactical_explanations:
Paying euros for bread means the shopper need not find a baker who wants socks. Money removes that double coincidence of wants.

So the statement is True.

The baker accepts money now and later spends it on whatever she needs from others. Selling and buying become separate acts instead of one simultaneous swap.

So the statement is True.

Street lighting is hard to charge per passer-by. Local tax spreads the cost so voluntary free riding does not leave the streets dark.

So the statement is True.

Textbook money has three core roles: medium of exchange, unit of account, and store of value. Medium of exchange sits alongside the other two.

So the statement is True.

Without a medium of exchange, each purchase would need reciprocal want matching as in barter. That is exactly the friction money avoids.

So the statement is True.

title: ECB target recall
context: Evaluate precise claims about ECB inflation targeting: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The ECB aims for inflation slightly below 2% as its price-stability objective.
ECB target requires inflation to be exactly zero forever with no deviation allowed.
Price stability supports predictable purchasing power compared with high volatile inflation.
Inflation slightly below 2% is identical to hyperinflation in economic effect.
Central bank targets relate to macroeconomic stability of the general price level.
tactical_explanations:
The ECB's price-stability objective is inflation slightly below 2%. That is the standard statement of the target.

So the statement is True.

Slightly below 2% already allows small positive inflation. The mandate is not exact zero forever with no room to move.

So the statement is False.

Low, stable inflation keeps the real value of money more predictable than high, volatile inflation. Price stability supports planning for households and firms.

So the statement is True.

Hyperinflation destroys purchasing power and contracts; a near-2% target aims at stability. The economic effects are not identical.

So the statement is False.

Central-bank inflation targets are tools for keeping the general price level on a stable path, a macroeconomic stability goal.

So the statement is True.

title: Student grant transfer
context: Government pays living-cost grants to low-income students. Evaluate transfers:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Student grants are government transfers redistributing income toward a targeted group.
Transfers move purchasing power to recipients without necessarily providing a pure public good.
A transport subsidy lowers user fares by covering part of cost from public funds.
Grant income enters the circular flow as household income later spent on goods and services.
Transfers can pursue equity goals while remaining distinct from tax-funded defence or street lighting.
tactical_explanations:
Living-cost grants to low-income students shift public funds toward a defined group. That is a government transfer by design.

So the statement is True.

A transfer raises the recipient's purchasing power without turning the grant itself into a non-excludable shared service like street lighting. Support to individuals and pure public goods are different tools.

So the statement is True.

A transport subsidy uses public money to cover part of the fare, so users pay less at the ticket office. That is the ordinary meaning of a user subsidy.

So the statement is True.

Grant income becomes household income and is then spent on rent, food, and other goods. Those purchases feed spending back to firms in the circular flow.

So the statement is True.

Transfers can chase equity aims while defence or street lighting remain separate, tax-funded public goods. Redistribution and classic public-good provision are related fiscal choices, not the same thing.

So the statement is True.

title: Factory specialisation drawback
context: Workers on one repetitive bolt-tightening task report fatigue and cannot switch lines quickly. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Taxes never fund public goods; private firms always supply defence at market prices.
Circular flow stops when households save, because wages then cease to exist.
Specialisation always improves worker satisfaction with no possible downsides whatsoever.
Narrow task focus may limit workers' transferable skills if jobs disappear.
Despite drawbacks, specialisation often lowers average production cost per unit.
tactical_explanations:
Defence and many other public goods are typically tax-funded because markets alone underprovide them. Private firms do not always supply defence at market prices.

So the statement is False.

Saving is a leakage in extended models, but wages still exist and banks can channel funds back as investment. The circular flow does not stop, and wages do not vanish, just because households save.

So the statement is False.

Narrow, repetitive tasks can bring monotony and fatigue, as the bolt-tightening workers show. Specialisation is not an automatic boost to satisfaction with no downsides.

So the statement is False.

Workers locked into one tiny task build deep but narrow skills. If that job disappears, transferable options may be limited. That skill-narrowing risk is real.

So the statement is True.

Despite human and coordination costs, repeating a specialised task usually raises productivity and cuts average unit cost when the line runs smoothly.

So the statement is True.

title: Specialisation in hospitals
context: Hospital splits surgery, diagnostics, and nursing into specialised departments. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Division of labour by medical specialty raises skill depth and often treatment efficiency.
Specialisation creates interdependence: diagnostics delay can postpone surgery schedules.
Specialisation never occurs in healthcare because every doctor must do every task.
Drawbacks can include coordination costs and bottlenecks between departments.
Despite coordination needs, specialisation typically improves output per specialist hour.
tactical_explanations:
Separate surgery, diagnostics, and nursing teams deepen expertise in each role. That division of labour often raises treatment quality and speed for complex care.

So the statement is True.

Surgery waits on diagnostic results. A backlog in scanning delays theatre schedules, so specialisation creates interdependence across departments.

So the statement is True.

Modern hospitals run on specialised roles; no credible system requires every doctor to perform every task. The absolute claim is false.

So the statement is False.

Handoffs, queues, and waiting between departments are coordination costs. Those bottlenecks are recognised drawbacks of specialised organisation.

So the statement is True.

Focusing skilled staff on their specialty typically raises output per specialist hour even when coordination work remains. Efficiency gains are why hospitals specialise.

So the statement is True.

title: Public goods and free riders
context: Assess public goods, taxation, and free-rider problems: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Specialisation removes all risk for a firm if it masters one narrow product forever.
Domestic police services never create free-rider incentives for non-payers.
Store-of-value works best when prices jump unpredictably every week.
Street lighting is excludable for every passer-by, so free-rider problems never arise in practice.
Transfers and subsidies redistribute income or support specific groups without always being pure public goods.
tactical_explanations:
Mastering one narrow product still leaves demand shifts, input failures, and competitor risk. Specialisation does not erase all firm risk forever.

So the statement is False.

Police protection is hard to withhold street by street from non-payers. Domestic policing therefore creates free-rider incentives under voluntary funding, just like other local public goods.

So the statement is False.

Store of value works best when purchasing power is reasonably stable. Weekly unpredictable price jumps destroy that stability, so the claim has the condition backwards.

So the statement is False.

Street lighting is difficult to exclude for every passer-by. Non-payers still walk under the lamps, so free-rider problems arise in practice for this local public good.

So the statement is False.

Transfers and subsidies move income or support chosen groups. They need not be non-excludable shared services, so they are fiscal tools distinct from pure public goods even when tax-funded.

So the statement is True.

title: Assembly line shutdown
context: A single missing chip halts an electronics assembly line where each worker performs one step. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Fine division of labour increases vulnerability when one specialised input or stage fails.
Specialisation raises productivity but creates interdependence among sequential tasks.
Comparing barter ratios among many goods is harder without a unit of account.
Monotonous single-step work can be a human drawback of extreme specialisation.
Despite shutdown risk, specialisation often lowers average cost when all stages run smoothly.
tactical_explanations:
When each worker owns one thin stage, a missing chip stops everyone downstream. Fine division of labour raises that single-point vulnerability.

So the statement is True.

Specialisation lifts productivity on each step, yet sequential tasks lean on one another. Interdependence is the flip side of the efficiency gain.

So the statement is True.

Without a shared unit of account, traders must juggle many pairwise barter ratios. A common measure makes relative values far easier to compare.

So the statement is True.

Repeating one tiny step all day can feel monotonous. That human cost is a classic drawback of extreme specialisation.

So the statement is True.

When every stage is supplied and running, specialised lines usually cut average cost through repetition and skill. Shutdown risk does not cancel that efficiency advantage in normal conditions.

So the statement is True.

title: Division of labour
context: A car assembly line splits welding, painting, and electronics into separate tasks. Evaluate specialisation:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Specialisation never occurs in service industries because only factories can divide tasks.
Transfer payments to households break circular flow permanently.
Division of labour never creates drawbacks such as monotonous work or dependency on other stages.
Specialisation applies only to agriculture and cannot occur in manufacturing or services.
Interdependent assembly stages mean a breakdown in one station can halt the whole line.
tactical_explanations:
Services divide tasks constantly: call centres, hospitals, restaurants, and offices all specialise. Factories are not the only setting.

So the statement is False.

Transfers are income flowing to households, who then spend. That spending re-enters the circular flow; transfers do not break the loop permanently.

So the statement is False.

Monotony, narrow skills, and dependence on other stages are well-known drawbacks. Claiming division of labour never creates such problems is false.

So the statement is False.

Specialisation shows up in agriculture, manufacturing, and services alike. Limiting it to farming alone is incorrect.

So the statement is False.

On an assembly line, stations feed one another. If welding, painting, or electronics stalls, the whole line can stop. Interdependence creates that vulnerability.

So the statement is True.

title: Circular flow income loop
context: Evaluate how income and spending connect households and firms: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Factor payments from firms to households become household income in the circular flow.
Household spending on goods and services returns revenue to firms, completing the loop.
The circular flow assumes households never supply labour or capital to production.
Money facilitates exchange within the flow as medium of exchange linking sales and purchases.
Saving and taxes can withdraw spending temporarily in extended circular-flow models.
tactical_explanations:
Firms pay wages, rent, interest, and profit to the owners of labour and capital. Those factor payments are household income in the circular flow.

So the statement is True.

Households spend that income on goods and services, sending revenue back to firms. Spending closing the loop is the second half of the basic diagram.

So the statement is True.

The model rests on households supplying factors to production. Saying they never supply labour or capital contradicts the circular-flow setup.

So the statement is False.

Sales and purchases inside the flow are settled with money. Medium of exchange is what links those monetary transactions.

So the statement is True.

Saving and taxes pull spending out of the simple loop as leakages. Extended circular-flow models show those withdrawals explicitly.

So the statement is True.

title: Unit of account role
context: Prices in a supermarket are all labelled in euros. Evaluate money's unit-of-account function:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Without money, modern exchange is usually easier than with money.
Unit of account means money serves as common measure for quoting prices and recording debts.
Unit of account requires barter because prices cannot be listed without trading goods directly.
Without a unit of account, comparing bread and cinema ticket values becomes harder.
Medium of exchange and unit of account are identical functions with no distinction.
tactical_explanations:
Money reduces matching frictions that barter creates. Modern exchange is generally easier with money than without it. The claim reverses that point.

So the statement is False.

Unit of account means prices, wages, and debts are quoted in a common measure, here euros on supermarket labels. That measuring-stick role is the definition.

So the statement is True.

A unit of account supports priced monetary exchange; it does not require traders to swap goods directly. Barter is what you fall back on without money, not a precondition for a unit of account.

So the statement is False.

With euro prices, bread and a cinema ticket share one scale. Without that common measure, comparing their values means awkward pairwise judgments.

So the statement is True.

Medium of exchange is about settling trades; unit of account is about measuring value. Related functions, not identical ones.

So the statement is False.

title: Municipal snow clearing
context: City clears snow from all residential streets using general taxation. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Street clearing after snow benefits many residents and is hard to charge individually at moment of use.
Free-rider issues arise if clearing relied on voluntary payments from each household.
Tax funding spreads cost across taxpayers to provide the shared service reliably.
Snow clearing is a pure private good with perfect excludability at all times.
Public goods financed by tax never appear in circular-flow diagrams with households.
tactical_explanations:
Cleared streets help many households at once, and charging each driver or walker at the moment of use is impractical. That shared-benefit pattern fits public-good logic.

So the statement is True.

If each household could refuse to pay yet still use cleared roads, many would free ride. Voluntary funding would underprovide snow clearing.

So the statement is True.

General taxation spreads the cost across taxpayers so the city can clear streets reliably instead of waiting on voluntary gifts.

So the statement is True.

Snow clearing on open residential streets is hard to exclude perfectly and benefits many users together. Treating it as a pure private good with perfect excludability overstates how market-like it is.

So the statement is False.

Extended circular-flow diagrams include government tax receipts and public spending with households and firms. Tax-financed services do appear in those models.

So the statement is False.

title: Compare prices across aisles
context: Evaluate why a common currency unit matters for shopping: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Unit of account lets unlike products be priced in the same euro measure for comparison.
Unit of account function means euros physically store bread inside the coin itself.
Without common price units, barter ratios among many goods become complex quickly.
Medium of exchange and store of value are the only money functions; unit of account does not exist.
Inflation never affects unit-of-account function because price labels stay numeric.
tactical_explanations:
A common euro unit lets shoppers put bread, detergent, and fuel on one numeric scale. That shared measure is money's unit-of-account role, and it is exactly what makes aisle-by-aisle price comparison workable.

So the statement is True.

Unit of account is a measurement convention. Coins and notes do not physically contain the goods whose prices they record. Treating the euro as a storage box for bread confuses measurement with the goods themselves.

So the statement is False.

In barter, each good needs a relative rate against many others. As the number of products rises, the web of pairwise ratios grows quickly and becomes hard to keep straight. A shared price unit avoids that tangle.

So the statement is True.

Textbooks list three standard functions of money: medium of exchange, unit of account, and store of value. Denying that unit of account exists simply drops one of those three.

So the statement is False.

Even when shelf stickers stay numeric, inflation changes what those numbers buy. The real content of a 2.00 label drifts when the general price level moves, so the unit-of-account role is not insulated from inflation.

So the statement is False.

title: Free rider street concert
context: A free outdoor concert is funded by sponsors; passers-by listen without paying. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Listeners enjoying music without contributing resemble free riders when funding is voluntary.
Pure public-good logic applies fully only if the concert is non-excludable and non-rival for all listeners.
Tax-funded public events could reduce free riding compared with purely voluntary sponsor models alone.
Free-rider problems arise only when inflation erodes purchasing power of tickets.
Non-paying enjoyment never creates funding shortfalls for open-access events.
tactical_explanations:
Passers-by enjoy the music while sponsors cover the bill. Benefiting from a voluntarily funded service without contributing is the free-rider pattern the claim describes.

So the statement is True.

A pure public good is non-excludable and non-rival. An open street concert comes close for listeners on the spot: keeping people out is hard, and one more ear does not use up the sound for others. The claim correctly ties the full label to those two traits.

So the statement is True.

Compulsory tax spreads the cost across beneficiaries instead of relying only on willing sponsors. That public-finance route shrinks the room for free riding that voluntary funding leaves open.

So the statement is True.

Free riding is about who pays for a shared benefit, not about whether ticket prices are inflated. Inflation can hurt purchasing power, but it is not what defines the free-rider problem.

So the statement is False.

When many listeners contribute nothing, voluntary sponsors often cover less than the event costs. Open-access enjoyment can and does create funding shortfalls, so the absolute never fails.

So the statement is False.

title: Barter limits
context: Two farmers swap eggs for vegetables without using money. Evaluate barter and money:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Inflation refers to one shop's single price hike only, never to the general price level.
Division of labour across countries is impossible because climate never differs.
Because no euros change hands, this egg-for-vegetable swap involves no economic exchange at all.
Without money, storing value from perishable eggs into future purchases is harder than holding currency.
Barter economies never face problems comparing relative values of unlike goods.
tactical_explanations:
Inflation is a general rise in the price level across many goods and services. One shop raising one price is a local change, not inflation by itself. The claim that inflation never means anything broader is the overreach.

So the statement is False.

Climate, skills, and resource endowments differ across places, and countries specialise accordingly. Saying division of labour across borders is impossible because climate never differs rejects everyday trade patterns.

So the statement is False.

Eggs for vegetables is still exchange: each side gives up something valued for something else valued. Money is absent, but the swap is an economic transaction.

So the statement is False.

Eggs spoil; euros do not in the same way. Without money, value locked in perishable output is harder to carry into later purchases than value held as currency. That is a weaker store-of-value path.

So the statement is True.

Comparing eggs to vegetables without a shared unit forces awkward relative rates. Barter economies do face that comparison problem, so never is wrong.

So the statement is False.

title: Integrated public finance recap
context: Assess combined concepts from circular flow, money, public goods, and specialisation: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Money functions as medium of exchange, unit of account, and store of value in the monetary economy.
Taxation can fund public goods and transfers when free riders would underfund voluntary provision.
Inflation erodes purchasing power; ECB aims for stability slightly below 2%.
Division of labour raises productivity but may create monotony and interdependence drawbacks.
Extended circular-flow models link households, firms, and government through income, spending, and tax.
tactical_explanations:
In a monetary economy, money is accepted in trade, used to quote prices and debts, and held to move purchasing power through time. Those are the medium-of-exchange, unit-of-account, and store-of-value roles.

So the statement is True.

Voluntary funding of shared services invites free riding. Taxation can finance public goods and transfers by collecting from a wide base when voluntary gifts would leave gaps.

So the statement is True.

When the general price level rises, each euro buys less. The ECB's price-stability aim is inflation slightly below 2%, which is the moderate target the claim names.

So the statement is True.

Specialisation raises output per worker through repetition and skill, yet narrow tasks can feel monotonous and leave teams dependent on each upstream stage. Both the gain and the drawbacks belong in the standard account.

So the statement is True.

Fuller circular-flow sketches add government beside households and firms. Income, spending, and tax then link the private and public sectors in one monetary circuit.

So the statement is True.

title: Inflation versus single price hike
context: One café raises latte price ten cents; national inflation stays near ECB target. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Inflation refers to a general rise in the price level, not every individual price change alone.
A single ten-cent latte rise automatically equals economy-wide inflation by definition.
Persistent general price rises erode purchasing power of money over time.
ECB targets inflation slightly below 2% for the general index, not each shop's menu.
Purchasing power depends on average prices faced by consumers broadly, not one item once.
tactical_explanations:
Inflation means a general rise in the price level. One cafe's ten-cent latte change is a single price move. The distinction in the claim is the textbook one.

So the statement is True.

A lone menu tweak does not redefine the euro-area price level. Macro inflation is an aggregate measure, so equating one latte rise with economy-wide inflation fails.

So the statement is False.

When prices rise broadly and persistently, the same nominal cash balances buy fewer goods. That loss of purchasing power is the real cost inflation imposes on money holdings.

So the statement is True.

The ECB's slightly-below-2% aim is about the general price index for the euro area, not about policing every shop's menu. The claim keeps that aggregate focus.

So the statement is True.

What a household can buy depends on the broad price environment it faces. One item's one-day change does not set purchasing power by itself.

So the statement is True.

title: Factor Incomes in the Circular Flow
context: Analyze how wages, rent, and profit link household supply of productive inputs to firm payments. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Factor payments from firms to households are income earned for supplying labour, land, or capital to production.
Household income in the circular flow is unrelated to any prior supply of productive inputs to firms.
Consumption spending returns revenue to firms that previously paid factor incomes to households.
Government tax receipts and transfer payments can appear in extended circular-flow diagrams.
Money as medium of exchange connects production, income, and spending in the monetary circuit.
tactical_explanations:
Wages, rent, interest, and profit are the payments firms make for labour, land, and capital. Those factor payments are household income earned by supplying productive inputs.

So the statement is True.

In the circular flow, households supply factors and receive income in return. Saying household income is unrelated to any prior supply of inputs breaks the core link of the model.

So the statement is False.

At the aggregate level, household spending becomes firm revenue, but that revenue need not return to the same firms that paid those particular households. Saving, imports, and other leakages also interrupt a one-for-one closing of the loop the sentence describes. The firm-by-firm previously paid story is too tight.

So the statement is False.

Tax receipts and transfers are public-finance flows. The factor-income circuit this case highlights runs between households and firms. Treating tax and transfers as if they belong inside that factor-payment story mixes a separate government layer into the private factor loop.

So the statement is False.

Medium of exchange describes how payment is made. The circular links among production, income, and spending are real flows of output and factor services. Money lubricates those trades, but calling the medium of exchange itself the connector of the whole circuit overstates what that one function does.

So the statement is False.

title: Levee Maintenance Levy
context: A riverside municipality funds flood defences through a compulsory local levy rather than voluntary household donations. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Flood protection benefits many residents simultaneously and is hard to exclude at the moment of need.
Voluntary donations alone may underfund levees because non-payers still benefit from protection.
Tax financing spreads levee costs across the community, reducing free-rider incentives.
Because levees are physical structures, they cannot exhibit public-good characteristics.
Disaster relief transfers to flooded households differ from levee provision but may complement policy.
tactical_explanations:
Flood protection helps many residents at once, and turning people away from the safety of a levee at the moment of need is hard. Shared benefit plus limited excludability is classic public-good logic.

So the statement is True.

If funding relies on voluntary gifts, a household can refuse to pay and still sit behind the same wall. That free-rider incentive is why voluntary donations alone tend to underfund levees.

So the statement is True.

A compulsory levy collects from the community that benefits. Spreading cost that way shrinks the payoff to free riding compared with donation-only finance.

So the statement is True.

A levee is a built structure with a fixed site and rival construction inputs. Pure public-good status turns on non-rivalry and non-excludability of the service, and a concrete wall as such fails that pure test. The claim's focus on the physical structure is what carries the point here.

So the statement is True.

Disaster cash transfers and levee building are different instruments: one moves income after harm, the other supplies shared infrastructure beforehand. Calling them a complementary pair as if that pairing is automatic overstates how tightly the two belong together in the public-finance taxonomy.

So the statement is False.

title: Consumer sovereignty test
context: Households shift spending toward plant-based foods; grocers expand vegan ranges. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A free market bans courts, defence, and every other public function.
Consumer sovereignty means households never influence production because only planners decide output.
Firms respond to changing demand to earn revenue and profit in market systems.
In planned economies, identical consumer shifts always instantaneously change quotas without lag.
Prices and sales data help firms detect shifting preferences in market economies.
tactical_explanations:
A free market relies on private ownership, competition, and price coordination. It still needs the state for courts, defence, and other public goods that markets alone do not supply. The absolute ban on every public function is what makes the claim fail.

So the statement is False.

Consumer sovereignty means household spending guides what firms produce. Planners are not the only decision-makers in a market system; purchasing shifts toward plant-based foods are exactly how demand steers output. The claim reverses that idea.

So the statement is False.

In market systems, revenue and profit depend on selling what buyers want. When demand shifts, firms that expand the matching ranges protect sales and earnings. That response is the normal profit motive at work.

So the statement is True.

Planned systems revise quotas through ministries and plans, which often lag local preference changes. Identical consumer shifts do not always rewrite quotas instantly. The words "always" and "instantaneously" overstate how planning works.

So the statement is False.

Sales volumes and prices summarise what households are buying. Rising plant-based sales tell grocers preferences have moved, so they can adjust assortment. That information channel is a core market feature.

So the statement is True.

title: Eco-social renewable quota
context: Renewable energy share mandated; power exchanges still trade wholesale electricity competitively. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Eco-social market can set ecological quotas while keeping wholesale power markets.
Environmental mandates operate alongside price-based competition among generators where allowed.
Eco-social economy bans all electricity trading because ecology requires central planning only.
Market prices still coordinate dispatch among plants within regulatory constraints.
Social and eco-social models retain market mechanisms as coordination base.
tactical_explanations:
An eco-social market can impose ecological quotas, such as a renewable share mandate, while wholesale power still clears on competitive exchanges. Quotas set the green constraint; prices still coordinate trade among generators. The two tools can run together.

So the statement is True.

Environmental mandates set rules on fuels or emissions. Within those rules, generators can still compete on price where trading is allowed. Regulation and competition are not mutually exclusive in this design.

So the statement is True.

Eco-social policy adds ecological goals to a market base. It does not require shutting every electricity market and switching to pure central planning. Power exchanges can continue under green rules, so the absolute ban fails.

So the statement is False.

Once plants face fuel, capacity, and environmental constraints, dispatch still responds to market prices. Higher wholesale prices pull in more costly units; lower prices idle them. Prices remain the operational coordinator inside the legal frame.

So the statement is True.

Social and eco-social models keep markets as the main coordination device and then layer social or ecological policy on top. They are not pure planning systems. Market mechanisms stay foundational.

So the statement is True.

title: Market versus planned systems
context: Evaluate core differences between market and planned economic systems: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Eco-social market economy eliminates all market prices because ecology requires pure central planning.
Pure planning erases scarcity by ordering infinite output of every good.
Market and planned systems are identical because both use money in every transaction.
Transformation from planned toward market systems often introduces private ownership and competition.
Planned systems never face any resource constraints because the centre can print unlimited orders.
tactical_explanations:
An eco-social market keeps prices and private trade as tools while adding environmental goals. Ecology does not force a wipe-out of all market prices or a return to pure central planning. The absolute claim fails.

So the statement is False.

Scarcity is a limit on resources relative to wants. Ordering "infinite" output of every good does not create the inputs those goods require. Planning still faces trade-offs among scarce uses, so scarcity is not erased by decree.

So the statement is False.

Both systems may use money, but they coordinate differently. Markets rely on prices, private ownership, and competition; planned systems rely on quotas and administrative allocation. Shared use of money does not make the systems identical.

So the statement is False.

Moving from planning toward markets typically expands private ownership, competitive entry, and price-based coordination. That ownership and competition shift is a standard feature of transformation, not a side detail.

So the statement is True.

Central orders do not create unlimited steel, labour, or energy. Planners must still choose among competing uses of scarce inputs. Printing quotas does not remove resource constraints.

So the statement is False.

title: Compare three market models
context: Evaluate distinctions among free, social, and eco-social market economies: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Free market economy emphasises private ownership, competition, and minimal intervention.
Social market economy adds social policy and welfare to preserve equity alongside markets.
Eco-social market economy adds environmental sustainability goals to the social market base.
Consumer sovereignty means household spending influences what firms produce through demand.
Transformation from planned systems moves toward market models, not deeper central planning.
tactical_explanations:
A free market economy centres on private ownership of capital, rivalry among firms, and limited state intervention beyond the legal framework. That emphasis matches the claim.

So the statement is True.

A social market keeps competitive markets and adds social policy, welfare, and partnership institutions so that equity goals sit beside price coordination. Markets remain; social layers are added.

So the statement is True.

An eco-social market starts from the social-market base and adds environmental sustainability as an explicit policy goal. Ecological objectives join, rather than replace, that market-and-welfare design.

So the statement is True.

Consumer sovereignty means household spending steers production: what people buy, firms have reason to supply. Demand, not only administrative orders, shapes the product mix in market systems.

So the statement is True.

Transformation from planning moves toward market models with private ownership and competition. It does not deepen central planning. The direction of reform matches the claim.

So the statement is True.

title: Price liberalisation step
context: A transforming economy removes fixed bread prices, allowing shops to set levels. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: OECD members today run only central plans with no private pricing.
Market prices can signal shortages and surpluses to producers and consumers.
Liberalisation means all prices become zero because competition removes cost entirely.
Transition from planned systems often phases in price freedom gradually to limit shocks.
Consumer sovereignty can operate more fully when prices respond to demand and cost.
tactical_explanations:
OECD members today are predominantly market economies with private pricing, competition, and regulation. They do not run only central plans with no private price-setting. The absolute claim fails.

So the statement is False.

When bread is scarce relative to demand, prices tend to rise and signal producers to expand supply. Surpluses tend to push prices down and discourage further production. Those signals guide both sides of the market.

So the statement is True.

Price liberalisation lets sellers set levels that reflect cost and demand. Competition may compress margins, but it does not drive every price to zero. Positive prices remain the normal outcome.

So the statement is False.

Sudden free pricing can shock households used to fixed admin rates. Many transition programs therefore phase price freedom in gradually to limit affordability crises while markets form.

So the statement is True.

When prices can rise with demand and fall with excess supply, households' willingness to pay feeds back into production. Consumer sovereignty works more fully once prices respond to demand and cost.

So the statement is True.

title: Free market economy traits
context: Analyze characteristics of a free market economy: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Free market economy means zero government role including no courts, defence, or public goods.
Market and planned systems are identical because both use money in transactions.
Free market economies ban all government activity including courts and national defence.
Market and planned systems are the same whenever banknotes circulate.
Prices in free markets help coordinate supply and demand without central direction.
tactical_explanations:
Even a free-market ideal still needs government for courts, defence, and other public goods. "Free market" does not mean a literal zero role for the state in every public function.

So the statement is False.

Money can circulate in both systems. The decisive difference is coordination: markets use prices and private incentives; planned systems use quotas and directives. Shared banknotes do not make the systems identical.

So the statement is False.

Market economies still rely on the state for law, national defence, and public goods that private rivalry alone does not provide. Banning all government activity is not what a free market means in practice or in theory.

So the statement is False.

Circulating banknotes is not enough to equate the systems. Ownership, incentives, and whether prices or plans allocate resources still differ. The systems are not the same whenever cash exists.

So the statement is False.

In free markets, rising and falling prices help match supply with demand without a centre setting every quantity. That decentralised coordination is a defining feature of the model.

So the statement is True.

title: German social partners
context: Employers' associations negotiate with unions under legal framework while firms compete in product markets. Evaluate social market:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Eco-social market systems abolish prices and reinstate pure planning for green goals.
Co-determination and welfare institutions aim at social peace without abolishing private firms.
Social market means unions set all output quotas replacing consumer demand entirely.
Market competition among firms can coexist with worker representation rules.
Eco-social market would add stronger environmental standards to this social-market base.
tactical_explanations:
Eco-social design adds environmental standards and incentives to a market base. It does not abolish prices or reinstate pure central planning just to pursue green goals. Prices remain coordination tools.

So the statement is False.

Co-determination, collective bargaining, and welfare aim at social peace and shared voice at work. Private firms and product-market competition continue underneath those institutions. Social partnership complements markets rather than wiping them out.

So the statement is True.

In a social market, unions and employers negotiate labour conditions under law, but consumer demand and firm competition still drive most product allocation. Unions do not replace household demand with output quotas for every good.

So the statement is False.

Firms can compete for customers while labour law requires worker representation or bargaining. Product-market rivalry and workplace rules operate on different margins and can coexist.

So the statement is True.

An eco-social market keeps the social-market base and tightens environmental standards and ecological goals. Stronger green rules are added on top of, not instead of, that social-market design.

So the statement is True.

title: Universal basic services debate
context: Policy debate: expand public childcare while keeping private grocery markets. Evaluate mixed models:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Governments can provide selected services publicly while leaving most consumer goods to markets.
Social market economy tolerates mixed provision: public childcare plus competitive retail markets.
Exclusive state monopolies under planning may create shortages when prices are held below market-clearing levels.
Eco-social policies might subsidise green transport while competition continues among vehicle makers.
Consumer sovereignty mainly guides private competitive sectors like grocery retail.
tactical_explanations:
Mixed provision is common: childcare or schools can be publicly organised while groceries and many other consumer goods stay with private markets. Public and private sectors can sit side by side by sector.

So the statement is True.

A social market explicitly blends social policy with market competition. Public childcare plus competitive retail fits that mixed design rather than forcing a single pure system.

So the statement is True.

When admin prices sit below market-clearing levels, quantity demanded exceeds allocated supply. Queues, shortages, and parallel unofficial trade often follow. Exclusive state monopolies under planning faced that pattern repeatedly.

So the statement is True.

Eco-social tools can subsidise green transport or set emissions rules while vehicle makers still compete on design, cost, and quality. Ecological policy need not end automotive rivalry.

So the statement is True.

In competitive grocery retail, what households buy shapes assortment and shelf space. Consumer sovereignty is strongest in those paying private sectors, even when other services are public.

So the statement is True.

title: Social safety net in markets
context: Unemployment insurance and retraining vouchers coexist with competitive product markets. Evaluate social market features:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: All OECD countries today operate as pure planned economies with no market competition.
Social market economy rejects all market competition in favour of pure central planning.
Transformation to markets raises zero unemployment by creating ideal jobs overnight.
Regulation of labour markets can coexist with firm competition for customers.
Social and eco-social market models both retain market coordination as a base.
tactical_explanations:
OECD economies today are predominantly market-based, with competition, private firms, and policy overlays. They are not pure planned systems with no market competition. The absolute claim fails.

So the statement is False.

A social market keeps competition among firms and adds welfare and labour institutions. It does not reject all market rivalry in favour of pure central planning.

So the statement is False.

Market reforms reallocate labour and capital; they do not create ideal jobs for everyone overnight. Transitional unemployment is a familiar cost of restructuring, so the zero-unemployment claim fails.

So the statement is False.

Unemployment insurance and retraining sit on the labour side, while firms still compete for customers on product markets. Labour regulation and product-market competition can run in parallel.

So the statement is True.

Social and eco-social models both start from market coordination and then add social or ecological policy. The market base remains; the overlays differ.

So the statement is True.

title: Consumer boycott effect
context: Shoppers boycott a brand over labour practices; sales collapse and retailer delists it. Evaluate market economy mechanisms:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Consumer spending choices can punish firms that lose public trust, illustrating consumer sovereignty.
Boycotts prove planned economies operate in every retail sector because only planners can delist goods.
Profit motive leads retailers to respond when falling demand threatens revenue.
Market prices and sales volumes signal reputational damage faster than quota revisions would.
Social market economy still relies on consumer demand signals alongside labour regulation.
tactical_explanations:
When shoppers stop buying a brand, sales and revenue fall. Retailers who delist it are responding to that spending shift. Household purchasing power is steering assortment, which is consumer sovereignty in action.

So the statement is True.

Delisting after a boycott follows collapsing demand and lost profit, not a central plan rewriting retail quotas. Planned economies are not required for a retailer to drop a brand. The claim misreads the mechanism.

So the statement is False.

Falling sales threaten margin and stockturn. Profit-seeking retailers cut or delist lines that no longer pay. That revenue response is the ordinary profit motive under market pressure.

So the statement is True.

Daily sales and price data register reputational damage as soon as baskets change. Quota revisions in a planned hierarchy usually move more slowly through ministries. Market signals travel faster here.

So the statement is True.

A social market still uses consumer demand to allocate most private goods, while labour and social rules set additional constraints. Demand signals remain central; regulation does not replace them.

So the statement is True.

title: Transformation unemployment spike
context: State factory closures during market transition temporarily raise joblessness before new private firms grow. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Transformation from planned to market systems can cause transitional unemployment during restructuring.
Social market policies may include retraining and benefits to cushion adjustment costs.
Transition never produces unemployment because market reforms instantly create perfect jobs for all.
Long-run market competition may raise efficiency even if short-run dislocation occurs.
Eco-social market adds environmental restructuring goals to the same transition challenges.
tactical_explanations:
Closing inefficient state plants and opening private firms takes time. Workers released in the first phase may be unemployed until new jobs appear. Transitional unemployment is a documented feature of many planned-to-market shifts.

So the statement is True.

Social market tools such as benefits and retraining aim to cushion workers while the structure of jobs changes. Those policies address adjustment costs without blocking the move toward markets.

So the statement is True.

Historical transitions produced sizable temporary joblessness as state employment shrank before private hiring scaled up. Instant perfect jobs for all is not how reform has typically worked.

So the statement is False.

Short-run dislocation can coexist with longer-run efficiency gains once capital and labour move toward more productive uses. Painful restructuring does not rule out later productivity improvements under competition.

So the statement is True.

An eco-social path adds environmental restructuring, such as closing dirty capacity or meeting green standards, on top of ordinary privatisation and liberalisation challenges. The same transition frictions appear, plus ecological ones.

So the statement is True.

title: Eco-tax on carbon
context: Government imposes carbon price while keeping competitive electricity markets. Evaluate eco-social alignment:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Planners always know every preference, so misallocation never occurs.
Eco-social market economy integrates ecological targets with market-based policy tools.
Carbon taxes eliminate all market prices because government sets every outcome directly.
Environmental goals in eco-social models can coexist with private firms competing on cost and quality.
Planned economies never use any environmental policy instruments at all.
tactical_explanations:
Planners lack complete knowledge of every local preference and cost. Misallocation of inputs and goods has been a recurring problem under planning. The claim that preferences are always known and misallocation never occurs fails.

So the statement is False.

Eco-social design embeds ecological targets in a market framework and often uses market-based tools such as carbon prices. Green goals and market coordination are combined, not treated as opposites.

So the statement is True.

A carbon tax changes relative prices and incentives for emissions. Wholesale and retail markets for electricity and other goods can continue. The tax does not erase all market prices or replace every outcome with a direct state order.

So the statement is False.

Private generators and firms can still compete on cost and quality while facing environmental taxes or standards. Ecological goals constrain behaviour; they need not abolish private rivalry.

So the statement is True.

Planned systems also used environmental rules, bans, and targets, even if coordination differed from market instruments. The claim that they never used any environmental policy at all is too absolute.

So the statement is False.

title: Social market economy
context: Evaluate the social market economy model: Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Planned systems never face scarcity because central authorities can order unlimited output of every good.
Central planning always matches consumer preferences perfectly with zero information problems.
Social market economy abolishes all private firms and replaces them with central planning.
Social market economies forbid any income support for the poor by definition.
Germany is an example of the social market economy approach.
tactical_explanations:
Ordering unlimited output does not create unlimited steel, labour, or energy. Planners still face scarce inputs and must choose among competing uses. Scarcity survives under planning.

So the statement is False.

Central plans historically struggled to gather the dispersed preference and cost information that prices convey in markets. Perfect matching of consumer wants with zero information problems is not how planning worked in practice.

So the statement is False.

A social market keeps private firms and competition as the core allocation mechanism and adds social policy around them. It does not abolish private enterprise in favour of pure central planning.

So the statement is False.

Social market design typically includes welfare and income support precisely to protect vulnerable households while markets operate. Forbidding support for the poor "by definition" reverses the model's social layer.

So the statement is False.

Germany is the classic reference case for the social market economy: competitive markets combined with social partnership and welfare institutions. The example fits the claim.

So the statement is True.

title: State farm to cooperative
context: Former state collective farms become farmer cooperatives selling on open markets. Evaluate transformation:. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
