statements: Free markets require the state to set every consumer price daily.
Market sales expose producers to consumer demand rather than fulfilment of plan quotas alone.
Transition always keeps 100% state ownership because privatisation never occurs in agriculture.
Profit incentive and price signals can guide crop choice after liberalisation.
Planned quota agriculture ignored local soil advantage because central targets overrode all information.
tactical_explanations:
Free markets let prices emerge from supply and demand, subject to general rules. They do not require the state to set every consumer price each day. Daily admin price-setting is the opposite of free pricing.

So the statement is False.

When cooperatives sell on open markets, revenue depends on what buyers will pay. That link replaces sole reliance on meeting plan quotas. Consumer demand becomes the commercial test.

So the statement is True.

Agricultural transitions often moved land and farms into private hands, cooperatives, or mixed forms. Keeping 100% state ownership forever is not what those reforms typically did.

So the statement is False.

After liberalisation, crop prices and expected profit guide what farmers plant. Higher returns pull acreage toward demanded crops; weak prices push it away. Price and profit signals steer crop choice.

So the statement is True.

Central quotas often ignored local soil, climate, and cost information because targets came from above. Market feedback after reform lets those local advantages matter again for what is grown.

So the statement is True.

title: Planned steel quota surplus
context: Central plan targets steel output above what machinery factories can absorb. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Overplanned output creates surpluses when downstream demand is not coordinated through prices.
Market systems use price declines to signal excess supply and reduce production profitably.
Profit motive encourages firms to economise and respond to paying customers in competitive markets.
Transformation introduces market feedback to reduce persistent mismatch of intersectoral output.
Scarcity still applies under planning; producing too much steel wastes scarce inputs.
tactical_explanations:
If the plan orders more steel than machinery plants can absorb, unsold steel piles up. Without price feedback linking sectors, upstream quotas can overshoot downstream use. That surplus is a coordination failure of planning.

So the statement is True.

In markets, excess supply tends to push prices down. Lower prices cut margins and discourage further output until the surplus is worked off. Price declines are the signal to shrink production.

So the statement is True.

Firms that waste inputs or ignore paying customers lose revenue and profit. Competition rewards economising and matching supply to demand. That incentive structure is the profit motive in competitive markets.

So the statement is True.

Market reforms replace rigid quota chains with prices and contracts between sectors. Persistent mismatches between steel and machinery demand become costly rather than administratively locked in. Feedback improves intersectoral balance.

So the statement is True.

Steel, energy, and labour used on surplus output cannot be used elsewhere. Overproduction still burns scarce resources even when the plan ordered the tonnage. Scarcity continues under planning.

So the statement is True.

title: Eco-social housing standard
context: Government sets energy-efficiency rules while builders compete on design and price. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Planned systems give households unlimited product choice by design.
Environmental standards aim at sustainability without eliminating private builders competing for buyers.
Eco-social model requires abolishing all housing markets and assigning homes by central plan only.
Regulation sets minimum ecological performance; markets still compete above that floor.
Social market and eco-social market both preserve market coordination as a foundation.
tactical_explanations:
Planned systems typically offered limited, assigned assortments rather than open-ended household choice. Unlimited product variety by design was not the historical pattern of planning.

So the statement is False.

Energy-efficiency rules set a green floor for buildings. Private builders can still compete on design, location, and price above that floor. Standards and rivalry coexist.

So the statement is True.

An eco-social model can keep housing markets while imposing ecological performance rules. It does not require abolishing all housing markets and assigning every home by central plan only.

So the statement is False.

Regulation fixes minimum ecological performance. Above that minimum, developers still differentiate on layout, finishes, and price. The market competes on the margin beyond the floor.

So the statement is True.

Both social and eco-social variants keep market coordination as the foundation and then add social or ecological policy. The market base is preserved in each case.

So the statement is True.

title: Markets as Exchange Mechanisms
context: Analyze how buyers and sellers interact through prices to allocate goods and services. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Voluntary exchange in a market occurs when both parties expect to gain from the trade.
A market requires face-to-face bargaining and excludes nationwide online listings.
A market exists only where a government agency sets every transaction price.
Prices in a market serve only as receipts and carry no information about scarcity.
Repair workshops cannot form a market because their output is intangible advice.
tactical_explanations:
A trade is voluntary only when each side expects to be better off after exchanging. That mutual expected gain is what brings buyers and sellers into a market transaction in the first place.

So the statement is True.

A market is any arrangement that brings willing buyers and sellers together. Online listings that connect people across a country still count, even when nobody bargains face to face.

So the statement is False.

Markets can clear through negotiated or posted prices set by private parties. Government agencies sometimes regulate or set prices, but that is not a requirement for a market to exist.

So the statement is False.

Prices do more than record a sale. They signal how scarce a good is relative to demand and guide how much buyers want and how much sellers offer.

So the statement is False.

Services such as repairs are traded for money just like goods. Intangibility does not stop buyers and sellers from forming a market.

So the statement is False.

title: Vienna Naschmarkt Stallholders
context: Consider a Vienna Naschmarkt stallholder who adjusts herb prices as weekend foot traffic and wholesale costs shift. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Weekend crowds willing to pay more can raise equilibrium price for fresh herbs at the stall.
A wholesale cost increase may reduce quantity supplied at each price unless the stall raises its selling price.
A price above equilibrium clears the stall faster because buyers prefer costlier herbs.
Nearby competing stalls remove all price constraints because each seller sets prices independently.
Rising Saturday demand forces the stallholder to cut prices to attract more visitors.
tactical_explanations:
Larger weekend crowds raise willingness to pay for herbs, which shifts demand right. With supply unchanged, the new intersection sits at a higher equilibrium price.

So the statement is True.

Higher wholesale costs make each bunch less profitable at the old selling price, so the stall offers fewer herbs at each price, a leftward supply shift. Raising the selling price can restore some of that incentive to sell.

So the statement is True.

A price above equilibrium leaves quantity supplied larger than quantity demanded, so stock piles up rather than clearing faster. Buyers do not prefer a higher price for its own sake.

So the statement is False.

Rival stalls give buyers substitutes. That competition constrains how high any one seller can push price, even when each stall posts its own list.

So the statement is False.

Stronger Saturday demand typically supports a higher equilibrium price, not an automatic cut. Cutting price would be the response to weak demand or surplus, not to a demand boom.

So the statement is False.

title: The Law of Demand
context: Analyze the inverse relationship between a good's price and the quantity buyers are willing to purchase. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The demand curve slopes downward because marginal buyers drop out as price increases.
Ceteris paribus means other demand shifters such as income are held constant when price changes.
Higher concert ticket prices increase quantity demanded because buyers treat tickets as prestige goods.
Lower coat prices reduce quantity demanded because buyers expect inferior quality.
The law of demand states that quantity demanded rises whenever price rises.
tactical_explanations:
As price rises, some buyers who were just willing to buy at the old price stop buying. Fewer buyers remain active, so quantity demanded falls and the demand curve slopes down.

So the statement is True.

To isolate the effect of own price on quantity demanded, other determinants such as income, tastes, and related prices must be held fixed. That is what ceteris paribus means in the law of demand.

So the statement is True.

Holding other factors fixed, a higher ticket price reduces quantity demanded along the demand curve. Prestige or taste changes would be separate demand shifters, not the own-price effect itself.

So the statement is False.

Other things equal, a lower coat price raises quantity demanded. Quality concerns would be a taste or information shift, not the usual own-price movement along demand.

So the statement is False.

The law of demand says that, other things equal, quantity demanded falls when price rises, and rises when price falls. The claim reverses that relationship.

So the statement is False.

title: Demand Schedules and Curves
context: Review how a demand schedule maps prices to quantities and traces a downward-sloping demand curve. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Quantity demanded refers to a specific amount at a specific price, not the entire curve.
Plotting a demand schedule yields an upward-sloping curve matching the law of supply.
A demand schedule lists quantities suppliers would offer at successive prices.
Movement along a demand curve results from a change in consumer income.
Quantity demanded remains fixed at every price because buyers must purchase essentials.
tactical_explanations:
Quantity demanded is one price-quantity pair on the curve. Demand names the whole schedule of those pairs across prices.

So the statement is True.

A demand schedule plots as a downward-sloping curve: higher price, lower quantity demanded. An upward slope is the usual shape of supply, not demand.

So the statement is False.

A demand schedule records how much buyers would purchase at each price. What sellers would offer belongs on a supply schedule.

So the statement is False.

A change in income shifts the entire demand curve. Movement along the curve comes from a change in the good's own price, holding other determinants fixed.

So the statement is False.

Even for essentials, quantity demanded typically falls if price rises enough. Buyers economise, substitute, or buy less when the good becomes dearer.

So the statement is False.

title: Innsbruck Ski Equipment Hire
context: Consider an Innsbruck ski-hire shop that raises daily rental rates during peak holiday weeks. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Heavy snowfall forecasts can shift demand rightward for hire equipment independently of the posted daily rate.
Higher rental rates increase quantity demanded because holiday visitors budget more for equipment.
Competing discounts nearby leave quantity demanded unchanged because customers ignore substitutes.
Charging above equilibrium clears inventory faster because customers prefer scarce rentals.
Peak-season demand shifts always lower equilibrium rental rates to attract tourists.
tactical_explanations:
Snowfall forecasts change how valuable skiing looks this week. That non-price factor raises quantity demanded at each rental rate, shifting the demand curve right without needing a change in the posted price itself.

So the statement is True.

Holding other factors fixed, a higher rental rate reduces quantity demanded along the demand curve. Holiday budgets may shift demand, but that is a separate change, not the own-price effect of a rate increase.

So the statement is False.

Cheaper rivals are substitutes. At the shop's unchanged rate, some customers switch away, so quantity demanded at that shop falls.

So the statement is False.

A price above equilibrium creates surplus: more gear offered than customers take at that rate. Stock sits, it does not clear faster.

So the statement is False.

A rightward peak-season demand shift with limited supply raises equilibrium rental rates. Lower rates are not the usual result of stronger demand.

So the statement is False.

title: The Law of Supply
context: Analyze the direct relationship between a good's price and the quantity producers are willing to offer. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The law of supply states that, other things equal, quantity supplied rises when price rises.
The supply curve slopes upward because buyers demand more whenever sellers cut output.
At low prices producers supply maximum output to recover fixed costs quickly.
Movement along a supply curve reflects a change in technology holding price fixed.
Higher wheat prices reduce quantity supplied because farming costs rise with crop value.
tactical_explanations:
Other things equal, a higher market price makes extra production more rewarding, so producers offer a larger quantity. That direct price-quantity link is the law of supply.

So the statement is True.

The upward slope comes from sellers offering more when price rises. Buyer demand behaviour belongs on the demand side and does not define why supply slopes up.

So the statement is False.

At very low prices, covering variable costs becomes harder, so quantity supplied tends to be small, not maximal. Producers do not pour out maximum output when the selling price is unattractive.

So the statement is False.

A technology change shifts the whole supply curve. Movement along the curve comes from a change in the good's own price, with other supply determinants held fixed.

So the statement is False.

Other things equal, higher wheat prices raise quantity supplied. Cost rises that track input prices are a separate supply shift, not the own-price law of supply.

So the statement is False.

title: Supply Schedules and Curves
context: Review how a supply schedule maps prices to quantities and traces an upward-sloping supply curve. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Plotting a supply schedule yields an upward-sloping curve in price–quantity space.
Quantity supplied and supply are identical terms for the entire curve.
Producers supply less at higher prices because profit margins shrink on every unit.
A supply schedule lists quantities buyers would purchase at successive prices.
A price increase shifts the entire supply curve leftward without changing quantity supplied.
tactical_explanations:
A supply schedule pairs higher prices with larger quantities offered. Plotted, those pairs trace an upward-sloping supply curve.

So the statement is True.

Quantity supplied is one point on the curve at a given price. Supply names the whole relationship across prices. The terms are not interchangeable.

So the statement is False.

Other things equal, higher prices raise the incentive to offer more units, so quantity supplied rises. Margins typically improve with price when costs are unchanged.

So the statement is False.

Buyer purchase plans belong on a demand schedule. A supply schedule lists how much producers are willing to offer at each price.

So the statement is False.

A rise in the good's own price moves the market along the existing supply curve to a larger quantity supplied. A leftward shift would require a change in a non-price supply determinant.

So the statement is False.

title: Graz Bakery Morning Rush
context: Consider a Graz bakery that bakes extra bread before dawn when a nearby office tower schedules early meetings. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: When supply and demand intersect, the bakery neither systematically runs out nor piles up unsold rolls.
Early office meetings shift supply rightward because bakeries open earlier without demand changing.
A flour price spike shifts demand rightward because customers seek cheaper carbohydrates.
Pricing above equilibrium sells out faster because customers interpret higher price as higher quality.
Higher bread prices reduce morning output because expensive flour discourages baking.
tactical_explanations:
At the intersection, quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. Plans match, so the bakery is not systematically short of rolls or left with a lasting pile of unsold ones.

So the statement is True.

Early meetings raise office workers' willingness to buy morning bread, which is a demand shift. Opening earlier may help meet that demand, but the driver is not a supply shift with demand unchanged.

So the statement is False.

Dearer flour raises bakers' costs and shifts supply left. Customer demand for bread does not jump right simply because an input got costlier.

So the statement is False.

A price above equilibrium creates surplus: more baked than customers buy at that price. Stock lingers instead of selling out faster.

So the statement is False.

Other things equal, a higher bread price raises quantity supplied along the supply curve. Costlier flour is a separate leftward supply shift, not the own-price effect of dearer bread.

So the statement is False.

title: Market Equilibrium
context: Analyze the price and quantity at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Graphically, equilibrium occurs where the demand and supply curves intersect.
Equilibrium price is where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied in a market.
At equilibrium, there is no tendency for price to change from ongoing pressure of surplus or shortage.
Markets tend toward equilibrium as price adjustments reduce surplus or shortage.
The equilibrium quantity is the amount actually traded when supply matches demand.
tactical_explanations:
The demand and supply curves cross at one price-quantity pair. That intersection is the graphical picture of market equilibrium.

So the statement is True.

Equilibrium price is defined as the price at which buyers want exactly as much as sellers offer. Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied there.

So the statement is True.

With no surplus or shortage at that price, there is no immediate force from excess stock or unmet demand pushing price up or down.

So the statement is True.

When quantity demanded and quantity supplied diverge, price tends to rise or fall. Those adjustments shrink the gap and move the market toward equilibrium.

So the statement is True.

At equilibrium, the traded amount equals both quantity demanded and quantity supplied. That common quantity is the equilibrium quantity.

So the statement is True.

title: Adjusting Toward Equilibrium
context: Review how surpluses and shortages prompt price changes that move markets toward equilibrium. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: If price is below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, creating shortage.
A shortage at the current price puts upward pressure on price as buyers compete for limited goods.
A surplus at the current price puts downward pressure on price as sellers compete to attract buyers.
If price is above equilibrium, quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, creating surplus.
Competitive markets use price changes to coordinate plans when quantities demanded and supplied diverge.
tactical_explanations:
Below the equilibrium price, buyers want more than sellers offer at that price. The gap is a shortage.

So the statement is True.

When goods are scarce relative to demand at the posted price, buyers bid against each other. That competition pushes price up toward equilibrium.

So the statement is True.

Unsold stock means sellers are offering more than buyers take. To clear inventory, sellers cut price, which puts downward pressure toward equilibrium.

So the statement is True.

Above the equilibrium price, sellers offer more than buyers willingly purchase. The excess is a surplus.

So the statement is True.

When plans diverge, rising or falling prices change quantity demanded and quantity supplied until they meet again. Price is the coordination device.

So the statement is True.

title: Linz Rental Housing Listings
context: Consider Linz landlords listing flats who cut asking rents when units sit vacant for several weeks. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: At equilibrium rent, the number of vacant units neither grows nor shrinks persistently across weeks.
New apartment construction shifting supply rightward can lower equilibrium rent if demand stays fixed.
Cutting asking rent reduces quantity demanded because tenants prefer costlier apartments.
Vacant flats persisting for weeks prove asking rent is below equilibrium because tenants avoid cheap flats.
Heavy tenant competition always lowers equilibrium rent because landlords fear regulation.
tactical_explanations:
At equilibrium rent, quantity demanded matches quantity supplied. Listings neither accumulate week after week nor vanish into persistent shortage.

So the statement is True.

New construction adds rental units at each rent, shifting supply right. With demand fixed, the new intersection is at a lower equilibrium rent.

So the statement is True.

A lower asking rent raises quantity demanded along the demand curve. Tenants do not prefer higher rents for their own sake.

So the statement is False.

Flats sitting vacant for weeks mean quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at the asking rent. That is a surplus, which points to rent above equilibrium, not below it.

So the statement is False.

Strong tenant competition is excess demand at the current rent, which tends to push equilibrium rent up unless supply expands enough to offset it. Fear of regulation is not the standard market mechanism here.

So the statement is False.

title: Surplus in Product Markets
context: Analyze conditions where quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at a given price. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A surplus exists when quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at the prevailing price.
Surplus puts downward pressure on price because sellers compete to reduce excess stock.
Price above equilibrium is consistent with shortage because buyers crave expensive goods.
Rapid sell-outs and empty shelves typically signal a surplus at the current price.
A harvest bumper crop eliminates surplus because larger supply always matches demand exactly.
tactical_explanations:
Surplus is defined by that imbalance: at the going price, sellers offer more than buyers take.

So the statement is True.

Unsold stock leads sellers to shade price to attract buyers. That competition exerts downward pressure on price.

So the statement is True.

A price above equilibrium leaves quantity supplied larger than quantity demanded, which is surplus, not shortage. Buyers do not create shortage by craving higher prices.

So the statement is False.

Empty shelves and instant sell-outs mean buyers want more than is available at the posted price. That pattern signals shortage, while surplus shows up as lingering unsold stock.

So the statement is False.

A bumper harvest shifts supply right. At the old price, that can create surplus unless demand rises enough to match. Larger supply does not automatically clear the market.

So the statement is False.

title: Shortage in Product Markets
context: Review conditions where quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at a given price. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Long queues and rapid sell-outs often signal a shortage at the posted price.
A price ceiling set below equilibrium can create persistent shortage in a competitive market.
At a price below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied until price adjusts.
Shortage puts upward pressure on price as buyers compete for limited available units.
A shortage exists when quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at the prevailing price.
tactical_explanations:
Queues and goods vanishing quickly mean more people want to buy at the posted price than sellers can provide. That is the visible face of shortage.

So the statement is True.

A ceiling below equilibrium keeps price from rising to clear the market. Quantity demanded stays above quantity supplied, so shortage can persist.

So the statement is True.

Below equilibrium, buyers want more than is offered. The excess demand lasts until price rises (or some other adjustment restores balance).

So the statement is True.

When units are scarce relative to demand, buyers bid against each other. That competition pushes price upward.

So the statement is True.

Quantity supplied exceeding quantity demanded is surplus. Shortage is the opposite imbalance: quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.

So the statement is False.

title: Salzburg Festival Ticket Queue
context: Consider Salzburg festival-goers queuing overnight when discounted early-bird tickets sell out within minutes. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Minutes-long sell-outs at the posted price suggest quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
Overnight queues form when buyers expect shortage at the official price.
Persistent shortage forces resellers to cut prices below the sold-out official rate.
Adding extra performances shifts demand leftward because audiences dislike additional shows.
Raising the official ticket price increases shortage because fewer buyers withdraw.
tactical_explanations:
Tickets vanishing in minutes at the posted price means many more buyers want seats than the organiser is offering at that price. Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.

So the statement is True.

People line up overnight because they expect seats to run out at the official price. Queues are a response to anticipated shortage.

So the statement is True.

When official tickets are scarce at a low posted price, resale markets usually clear at higher prices, not below the sold-out rate. Scarcity supports a premium, not a forced cut.

So the statement is False.

Extra performances add seats, which is a rightward supply shift. Audience dislike of more shows is not the usual story, and demand does not shift left just because capacity expands.

So the statement is False.

A higher official price lowers quantity demanded along the demand curve and typically eases shortage. It does not enlarge the gap by keeping more buyers in the market.

So the statement is False.

title: Income as a Demand Shifter
context: Analyze how changes in consumer income shift demand for normal and inferior goods. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Income changes shift the entire demand curve rather than moving along it.
For inferior goods, rising income can shift demand leftward as buyers switch to higher-quality substitutes.
A recession reducing household income shifts demand rightward for discretionary electronics.
Higher consumer income shifts demand leftward for normal goods because buyers save everything.
A pay rise for office workers lowers equilibrium coffee price because richer buyers demand discounts.
tactical_explanations:
Income is a non-price determinant of demand. When income changes, quantity demanded at each price changes, so the whole curve shifts. Own-price changes alone move along a fixed curve.

So the statement is True.

Inferior goods lose buyers when incomes rise, as people trade up. Demand at each price falls, which is a leftward shift.

So the statement is True.

Discretionary electronics are typically normal goods. Lower household income reduces demand for them, shifting demand left, not right.

So the statement is False.

For normal goods, higher income raises demand at each price, a rightward shift. Buyers do not automatically save every extra euro and abandon the good.

So the statement is False.

A pay rise that raises coffee demand with supply fixed pushes equilibrium price up. Richer buyers do not force discounts through stronger demand alone.

So the statement is False.

title: Tastes and Preferences
context: Review how changing consumer tastes and preferences shift the demand curve. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Advertising that increases brand preference shifts demand rightward for the advertised good.
Seasonal fashion trends shifting tastes can change equilibrium clothing prices within a year.
A health trend favouring oat milk can shift demand rightward for oat beverages at each price.
When substitutes become fashionable, demand for the original good may shift leftward.
Negative publicity about a product shifts supply leftward because producers feel discouraged.
tactical_explanations:
Stronger brand preference raises how much buyers want at each price. That is a rightward demand shift for the advertised good.

So the statement is True.

Taste shifts move demand, and with a given supply that changes the intersection. Seasonal fashion can therefore move clothing equilibrium prices within a year.

So the statement is True.

A health-driven preference for oat milk raises quantity demanded at each price, shifting demand for oat beverages right.

So the statement is True.

If rivals become fashionable, some buyers leave the original good. Demand for it falls at each price, a leftward shift.

So the statement is True.

Negative publicity changes buyer willingness to purchase, which is a demand shift. Producer feelings do not turn publicity into a supply shifter by themselves.

So the statement is False.

title: Styrian Wine Tasting Boom
context: Consider a Styrian wine route that sees surging visitor numbers after international tasting awards. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Surging visitor demand with limited tour slots can create shortage at the posted tasting price.
Award publicity can shift demand rightward for regional wine tastings at unchanged ticket prices.
Higher equilibrium tasting fees may result if demand shifts right while supply remains constrained.
Raising tasting fees can reduce shortage by lowering quantity demanded along the demand curve.
Expanded visiting hours shift demand leftward because tourists dislike longer schedules.
tactical_explanations:
If many more visitors want slots than the route can offer at the posted fee, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied. That imbalance is a shortage.

So the statement is True.

Awards raise awareness and preference for Styrian tastings. At the same ticket prices, more people want to book, so demand shifts right.

So the statement is True.

A rightward demand shift with constrained supply moves the intersection to a higher equilibrium fee. Stronger demand meets limited capacity.

So the statement is True.

A higher fee reduces quantity demanded along the demand curve. That shrinks excess demand and can ease the shortage at the old low price.

So the statement is True.

Longer opening hours expand how many tours can be sold, which is a supply increase. Tourists do not typically demand fewer tastings simply because hours stretch.

So the statement is False.

title: Prices of Substitute Goods
context: Analyze how the price of substitute goods shifts demand for a related product. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Firms monitor substitute pricing because cross-price shifts alter their equilibrium sales.
Substitute price changes shift demand rather than causing movement along the demand curve.
Cheaper streaming subscriptions may shift demand leftward for cinema tickets.
Coffee shops see lower demand when nearby tea prices increase because beverages are complements.
A rise in petrol prices shifts demand leftward for public transport because travel becomes undesirable.
tactical_explanations:
When a substitute's price changes, demand for the firm's own product can shift, changing equilibrium quantity and price. Watching rival prices is therefore commercially relevant.

So the statement is True.

The substitute's price is a related-goods determinant. Its change shifts the demand curve. Movement along the curve comes only from the good's own price.

So the statement is True.

Streaming is a substitute for cinema visits. Cheaper subscriptions pull some viewers away, lowering demand for tickets at each cinema price.

So the statement is True.

Tea and coffee are substitutes, not complements. Dearer tea typically raises coffee demand as some drinkers switch, rather than lowering it.

So the statement is False.

Petrol and public transport are often substitutes for getting around. Higher petrol prices typically raise demand for buses and trains, a rightward shift, not a leftward one driven by travel becoming undesirable in general.

So the statement is False.

title: Prices of Complementary Goods
context: Review how the price of complementary goods shifts demand for a related product. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A rise in game console prices may shift demand leftward for compatible game titles.
When complements become costlier, equilibrium quantity of the paired good may fall.
Reduced air fares can shift demand rightward for airport parking and hotel rooms near terminals.
Lower printer prices can shift demand rightward for ink cartridges.
Complementary price changes shift demand for the related good, not supply directly.
tactical_explanations:
Consoles and compatible games are used together. Dearer consoles mean fewer platforms in homes, so demand for matching titles falls at each game price.

So the statement is True.

A leftward demand shift for the paired good, with supply unchanged, lowers the equilibrium quantity traded. Costlier complements can produce that outcome.

So the statement is True.

Cheaper flights encourage more travel, which raises demand for complementary services such as airport parking and nearby hotels.

So the statement is True.

Printers and ink are complements. Cheaper printers put more devices in use, raising demand for cartridges at each ink price.

So the statement is True.

Cross-price effects for complements change how much buyers want of the related good. That is a demand shift. It does not directly move the supply curve of the related good.

So the statement is True.

title: Electric Bus Fleet Procurement
context: Consider a municipal transport office comparing electric bus bids after diesel fuel costs spike. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher diesel costs can shift demand rightward for electric buses as substitutes become costlier.
A subsidy lowering effective purchase price shifts demand rightward for electric buses.
Expanded battery production shifting supply rightward can reduce equilibrium electric bus prices.
If electric bus prices stay fixed while demand shifts right, surplus appears at current contract offers.
At equilibrium contract price, manufacturers deliver buses cities refuse to operate.
tactical_explanations:
Diesel buses become more expensive to run when fuel spikes, so electric buses look relatively more attractive. Demand for electric buses rises at each purchase price.

So the statement is True.

A purchase subsidy lowers the effective price buyers face, so municipalities want more electric buses at each market list price. That is a rightward demand shift.

So the statement is True.

More battery capacity lowers production costs and increases quantity supplied at each bus price. With demand unchanged, equilibrium price falls.

So the statement is True.

If demand shifts right while price is stuck, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at that price. The imbalance is shortage, not surplus.

So the statement is False.

At an equilibrium contract price, quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. Systematic delivery of buses cities refuse to run would mean plans do not match, which is not equilibrium.

So the statement is False.

title: Input Costs and Supply
context: Analyze how changes in production costs shift the supply curve. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: When energy costs surge, equilibrium price may rise if demand remains unchanged.
Higher wages paid to warehouse staff can shift supply leftward for distribution services.
Cheaper imported components can shift supply rightward and lower equilibrium price.
Input cost changes move producers along the supply curve without shifting it.
A drop in steel prices shifts demand leftward because buyers expect weaker furniture.
tactical_explanations:
Higher energy costs shift supply left. With demand fixed, the new intersection is typically at a higher equilibrium price.

So the statement is True.

Wages are an input cost for distribution. Higher wages reduce quantity supplied at each service price, shifting supply left.

So the statement is True.

Cheaper components lower unit costs, so producers offer more at each price. Supply shifts right and, with demand unchanged, equilibrium price falls.

So the statement is True.

Input costs are supply shifters. They move the whole curve. Movement along the curve comes from a change in the product's own selling price.

So the statement is False.

Cheaper steel lowers producers' costs and shifts furniture supply right. It does not, by itself, shift demand left through weaker expected quality.

So the statement is False.

title: Technology and Productivity
context: Review how technological improvements shift supply by lowering production costs. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Technological progress that cuts unit cost shifts supply rightward, not leftward.
Improved irrigation technology may shift supply rightward for orchard fruit at each market price.
Automated sorting equipment can shift supply rightward for parcel delivery services.
Technology changes are supply shifters distinct from movements caused by the good's own price.
Rightward supply shifts from technology raise equilibrium price when demand is unchanged.
tactical_explanations:
Lower unit costs make production more profitable at each market price, so quantity supplied rises. That is a rightward supply shift, not a leftward one.

So the statement is True.

Better irrigation raises orchard productivity, so growers can offer more fruit at each price. Supply shifts right.

So the statement is True.

Automation that sorts parcels more cheaply raises quantity of delivery services offered at each price. Supply shifts right.

So the statement is True.

Technology changes the position of the supply curve. A change in the good's own price alone traces movement along a given curve.

So the statement is True.

With demand fixed, a rightward supply shift lowers equilibrium price. Technology-driven abundance does not raise the clearing price by itself.

So the statement is False.

title: Plant Capacity Expansion
context: Consider a manufacturing plant adding a production line that raises monthly output without raising unit prices. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: If demand stays fixed while supply shifts right, equilibrium price may fall.
At the new equilibrium, quantity traded may exceed the old equilibrium if demand is unchanged.
Higher raw-material input prices could partially offset the expansion by shifting supply leftward.
Customers ordering the product face lower shortage risk after a successful supply expansion.
Adding capacity that lowers unit cost can shift supply rightward for the manufactured good.
tactical_explanations:
A rightward supply shift with demand unchanged moves the intersection down the demand curve. Equilibrium price can fall.

So the statement is True.

The same rightward supply shift raises the equilibrium quantity when demand is fixed. More is traded at the new clearing point.

So the statement is True.

Dearer raw materials raise costs and shift supply left. That leftward push can partially cancel the rightward effect of the new line.

So the statement is True.

More capacity increases quantity available at prior prices, so excess demand is less likely. Shortage risk falls after a successful expansion.

So the statement is True.

Extra efficient capacity lowers unit cost and raises quantity supplied at each price. That is precisely a rightward supply shift.

So the statement is True.

title: Number of Sellers in a Market
context: Analyze how entry or exit of sellers shifts market supply. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: New bakeries opening on the same street shift supply rightward for local bread.
Exit of several suppliers during a crisis can create shortage at previously stable prices.
Entry of low-cost online retailers can lower equilibrium prices for standardised goods.
Farmers exiting a crop after poor seasons shift supply leftward for that harvest.
Market supply equals the largest individual seller's supply ignoring smaller rivals.
tactical_explanations:
Each new bakery adds loaves at each price. Market quantity supplied rises, so market supply shifts right.

So the statement is True.

When several suppliers leave, market supply shifts left. At the old stable prices, quantity demanded can exceed the smaller quantity supplied, producing shortage.

So the statement is True.

Low-cost entrants expand market supply. With demand roughly stable for standardised goods, equilibrium price tends to fall.

So the statement is True.

Fewer farmers growing the crop reduces market quantity supplied at each harvest price. That is a leftward supply shift.

So the statement is True.

Market supply aggregates every seller's offers at each price. Ignoring smaller rivals understates total supply.

So the statement is False.

title: Producer Expectations and Supply
context: Review how sellers' expectations about future prices influence current supply decisions. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: If producers expect costs to fall next month, some may delay production, shifting current supply leftward.
Expected future shortages motivate producers to halt current output entirely.
Expectations of higher future wheat prices increase current supply as farmers dump inventory.
Expectations about future conditions move producers along today's supply curve only.
Storage decisions based on future price outlook leave current market supply unchanged.
tactical_explanations:
If next month's costs look lower, producing later can be cheaper. Some output is postponed, so current quantity supplied falls at today's prices, a leftward shift.

So the statement is True.

Expecting future scarcity often encourages producers to produce more now, or at least keep supplying, rather than shut down entirely. Halting all current output is not the standard response.

So the statement is False.

If tomorrow's wheat price is expected to be higher, farmers often hold grain back for later sale. Current market supply tends to fall, not rise through dumping.

So the statement is False.

Expectations are a supply shifter. They change how much is offered at today's prices. Movement along today's curve comes from a change in today's own price.

So the statement is False.

Goods placed in storage are withheld from today's market. That storage choice reduces current supply relative to releasing the stock now.

So the statement is False.

title: Harvest Season Labour Contracts
context: Consider Styrian vineyards signing seasonal picker contracts before grape sugar levels peak. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Expectations of a large harvest can shift supply rightward for contract picker labour in August.
Timely contract signing before peak harvest can reduce later shortage when sugar levels spike.
If offered wages sit below equilibrium, vineyards may face shortage of available pickers.
Competing fruit regions raising wages may shift supply leftward for pickers in Styria.
Higher offered day rates typically increase the quantity of pickers willing to supply labour.
tactical_explanations:
A large expected harvest raises how many pickers vineyards want under contract at each wage. That non-wage change increases labour offered into the August contract market, which is a rightward supply shift for seasonal picker labour.

So the statement is True.

Contracts locked in early fix some labour before sugar levels spike and demand for pickers jumps. With more workers already secured, the gap between quantity demanded and quantity supplied at the rush is smaller, so shortage risk falls.

So the statement is True.

At a wage below the market-clearing level, employers want more labour than workers are willing to supply. Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, so vineyards can fail to fill all picker slots.

So the statement is True.

Higher wages in competing fruit regions pull workers away from Styria. At each Styrian wage, fewer pickers remain available locally, which is a leftward shift of Styrian labour supply.

So the statement is True.

The wage is the own-price of labour. Along an upward-sloping labour supply curve, a higher offered day rate raises the quantity of pickers willing to work, other things equal.

So the statement is True.

title: Simultaneous Demand and Supply Shifts
context: Analyze how concurrent shifts in demand and supply affect equilibrium price and quantity. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The net effect on equilibrium price depends on the relative size of demand and supply shifts.
Graphical analysis compares new intersection points to identify changed equilibrium outcomes.
If demand shifts right while supply shifts left, equilibrium price is likely to rise.
If demand shifts right and supply shifts right together, equilibrium quantity rises.
Supply and demand shifts can occur together after a natural disaster disrupts production and tastes.
tactical_explanations:
When demand and supply both move, each shift pushes price in its own direction. The final price change is therefore ambiguous until you compare how large the two shifts are.

So the statement is True.

Equilibrium is the intersection of demand and supply. After simultaneous shifts, the new curves cross at a different point, and that new intersection is what you read for the changed price and quantity.

So the statement is True.

A rightward demand shift raises willingness to pay at each quantity. A leftward supply shift cuts quantity offered at each price. Both forces push the clearing price up, so equilibrium price is likely to rise.

So the statement is True.

A rightward demand shift raises quantity traded at the new equilibrium. A rightward supply shift does the same. Together they raise equilibrium quantity even if the price change remains ambiguous.

So the statement is True.

A disaster can destroy capacity (supply left) while also changing what people want to buy (demand). Both curves can therefore move in the same period, not only one at a time.

So the statement is True.

title: Price Ceilings Below Equilibrium
context: Review how a legal maximum price set below equilibrium creates shortage in competitive markets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Non-price rationing such as queues may appear when ceilings create persistent shortage.
A ceiling set above equilibrium is not binding because market price stays below the cap.
Rent controls set below market equilibrium can leave landlords with fewer units to lease.
At the ceiling price, quantity supplied typically exceeds quantity demanded.
A price ceiling below equilibrium prevents price from falling to eliminate surplus.
tactical_explanations:
A binding ceiling keeps price below the clearing level, so quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied. When money price cannot allocate the scarce units, waiting lists, queues, or other non-price devices often appear.

So the statement is True.

If the legal maximum sits above the market-clearing price, sellers and buyers still meet below the cap. The ceiling never binds, so it does not change the equilibrium outcome.

So the statement is True.

Controlled rents below the open-market clearing level reduce the return on letting. Over time landlords may withdraw units or cut maintenance that keeps flats lettable, so fewer units remain available to lease.

So the statement is True.

A ceiling below equilibrium creates shortage: at the capped price, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied. The claim reverses that imbalance by saying supply exceeds demand.

So the statement is False.

A below-equilibrium ceiling blocks price from rising to clear shortage. Surplus is the opposite imbalance (excess supply), and the binding problem here is shortage, not surplus that needs a falling price.

So the statement is False.

title: Graz Rent-Control Apartment Search
context: Consider Graz tenants searching legacy rent-controlled flats while open-market leases advertise higher monthly rates. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Long waiting lists for controlled units signal excess demand at the regulated rent.
Controlled rents below open-market levels can create persistent shortage of available flats.
Landlords may redirect maintenance spending when regulated rents cover rising costs poorly.
Tenants ignore non-price costs when money rents stay capped because flats are abundant.
Open-market leases advertising higher rates prove equilibrium rent lies below the controlled cap.
tactical_explanations:
A long waiting list means more households want controlled flats than are available at the regulated rent. That is excess demand: quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at that price.

So the statement is True.

When the controlled rent sits below the open-market clearing rent, the cap binds. Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, so available controlled flats remain scarce over time.

So the statement is True.

If regulated rents lag rising costs, landlords earn a weaker return on upkeep. They may cut or redirect maintenance spending toward uses that pay better, which can worsen quality and availability.

So the statement is True.

At a binding low rent, flats are scarce, not abundant. Tenants still face search time, waiting lists, and other non-price costs even though the money rent is capped.

So the statement is False.

Open-market leases at higher rates show that the uncontrolled clearing rent lies above the controlled cap, not below it. The higher free-market ads place the equilibrium above the regulated rent.

So the statement is False.

title: Price Floors Above Equilibrium
context: Analyze how a legal minimum price set above equilibrium creates surplus in competitive markets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A price floor above equilibrium prevents price from falling to eliminate surplus.
Government purchase programs sometimes accompany agricultural price floors to absorb surplus.
At the floor price, quantity supplied typically exceeds quantity demanded.
A floor set below equilibrium is not binding because market price stays above the minimum.
Minimum prices intended to help sellers eliminate all unsold stock immediately.
tactical_explanations:
A floor above the clearing price leaves quantity supplied larger than quantity demanded. Price cannot legally fall to wipe out that excess supply, so the surplus persists.

So the statement is True.

Agricultural floors often create unsold output. Official purchase schemes buy the excess at the support price so the surplus is absorbed rather than left on the private market.

So the statement is True.

At a binding high minimum, sellers offer more than buyers want at that price. Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, which is surplus.

So the statement is True.

If the legal minimum sits below the market-clearing price, trade still occurs above the floor. The floor never constrains the price, so it is not binding.

So the statement is True.

A floor meant to help sellers can leave stock unsold because the high price creates surplus. Intent to protect sellers does not clear inventories immediately; the imbalance can remain.

So the statement is False.

title: Minimum Wage in Labour Markets
context: Review how a wage floor above equilibrium can create surplus labour supplied. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Labour markets use wages as prices coordinating workers' supply and employers' demand.
Employers reduce quantity demanded of labour when mandatory wages rise above equilibrium.
A minimum wage set below equilibrium is not binding for market outcomes.
A minimum wage above the market-clearing wage eliminates all unemployment immediately.
At a binding minimum wage, every worker willing to work finds employment instantly.
tactical_explanations:
Wages are the price of labour. They balance how much work people offer with how much employers want to hire, just as prices coordinate goods markets.

So the statement is True.

Labour demand slopes downward in the wage. When a mandated wage rises above the clearing level, employers move up that demand curve and hire fewer hours or workers.

So the statement is True.

If the legal minimum sits below the market-clearing wage, actual wages can still clear above the floor. The floor does not bind, so employment and wage outcomes stay at the market equilibrium.

So the statement is True.

A wage floor above the clearing wage creates surplus labour: more people want jobs than employers hire at that wage. That imbalance often shows up as unemployment, not the elimination of unemployment.

So the statement is False.

At a binding minimum wage, quantity supplied of labour exceeds quantity demanded. Not every willing worker finds a job; some remain unmatched at the floor.

So the statement is False.

title: Alpine Dairy Milk Quota Meeting
context: Consider an Alpine dairy cooperative setting a seasonal milk quota after feed costs jump and output surges. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher feed costs can shift supply leftward for raw milk at each farmgate price.
Cutting quota levels after a glut can help move the market toward equilibrium by reducing surplus.
If farmgate price stays fixed while feed costs rise, farmers expand output to celebrate.
A cooperative quota limiting deliveries increases quantity supplied by forcing extra production.
Surging milk output without matching demand creates shortage at the old farmgate price.
tactical_explanations:
Feed is an input. When feed costs jump, producing each litre is less profitable at a given farmgate price, so farmers offer less milk at each price. That is a leftward supply shift.

So the statement is True.

A glut means quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at the prevailing price. Tightening the quota cuts deliveries, shrinks the excess supply, and moves the market closer to balance.

So the statement is True.

With farmgate price fixed and feed costs higher, margins shrink. Farmers typically cut output that is no longer profitable; they do not expand production to celebrate.

So the statement is False.

A quota that limits deliveries caps how much milk may enter the market. It restricts quantity supplied; it does not force extra production or raise supply.

So the statement is False.

Extra milk at an unchanged demand and old farmgate price leaves more milk than buyers want. That imbalance is surplus (excess supply), not shortage.

So the statement is False.

title: Inflation as Rising Price Levels
context: Analyze inflation as a sustained increase in the overall price level across an economy. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Inflation is measured using price indices that track many goods and services together.
Central banks often monitor inflation when setting policies that influence interest rates.
Households purchasing the same basket notice inflation when that basket costs more over time.
Moderate inflation reduces the real purchasing power of money held without interest.
Inflation describes a one-day sale discount on a single retail product.
tactical_explanations:
Inflation is a rise in the general price level, not one item alone. Price indices average many goods and services so the measure tracks that broad movement.

So the statement is True.

Interest-rate and related monetary choices often respond to inflation data. Central banks therefore watch price indices when setting those policies.

So the statement is True.

If the same typical basket costs more month after month, households experience a higher general price level. That is how inflation shows up in everyday purchases.

So the statement is True.

When prices rise and cash earns no interest, each unit of money buys fewer goods. Real purchasing power of idle balances falls even under moderate inflation.

So the statement is True.

A one-day discount on a single product is a relative price cut, not a sustained rise in the overall price level. Inflation is economy-wide and persistent, not a shop-floor sale.

So the statement is False.

title: Too Much Money Chasing Goods
context: Review the explanation that inflation can result when too much money pursues available goods and services. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Inflation from monetary expansion differs from a single crop failure raising one food price.
If everyone spends newly printed money quickly, aggregate demand can rise faster than supply.
Inflation may accelerate when money supply growth outpaces growth in real output.
Holding other factors fixed, larger money supply reduces spending pressure on limited goods.
Too much money chasing too few goods explains deflation in monetary economics.
tactical_explanations:
A crop failure can spike one food price while other prices stay put. Monetary expansion that lifts spending across many markets raises the general price level. Those are different phenomena.

So the statement is True.

New money spent promptly adds to aggregate demand. If real supply cannot keep pace, that extra spending bids up prices across goods and services.

So the statement is True.

When money grows faster than real output, more nominal spending chases a slower-growing volume of goods. That imbalance tends to push the general price level up faster.

So the statement is True.

Holding other factors fixed, a larger money supply raises, not reduces, nominal spending power against limited goods. Spending pressure rises with the money stock in that setting.

So the statement is False.

"Too much money chasing too few goods" describes inflationary pressure from excess money relative to output. Deflation is a falling general price level, the opposite idea.

So the statement is False.

title: Central Bank Note-Issuance Debate
context: Consider policymakers debating faster note issuance to fund bridge repairs while shopkeepers report rising supplier invoices. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Shopkeepers reporting broadly rising supplier invoices suggest upward pressure on the price level.
Inflation erodes the real value of cash savings when prices rise faster than interest earned.
Funding repairs through new money may increase spending before additional goods and services appear.
Rapid note issuance without matching output growth can contribute to inflationary pressure.
Policymakers weighing note issuance must consider whether output can absorb extra spending.
tactical_explanations:
Supplier invoices rising across many shops point to a broad increase in costs and prices, not one isolated item. That pattern is upward pressure on the general price level.

So the statement is True.

Cash earns little or nothing while goods cost more. When prices rise faster than any interest on idle balances, each euro of savings buys less in real terms.

So the statement is True.

Financing repairs with newly issued notes puts spending power into the economy. That spending can arrive before bridges and related output expand, so demand may lead supply temporarily.

So the statement is True.

Fast note growth without matching real output growth means more money chasing a similar volume of goods. That gap feeds inflationary pressure on the price level.

So the statement is True.

Extra money raises spending only if goods can absorb it without large price jumps. Policymakers therefore ask whether capacity and output can meet the extra demand.

So the statement is True.

title: Interest Rates and Inflation Control
context: Analyze how raising interest rates can be used to reduce inflationary pressure. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher interest rates can reduce borrowing and spending, easing inflationary demand pressure.
Higher rates reward saving and can shift spending from today to later periods.
Interest rate increases operate partly by making loans for homes and equipment more expensive.
Monetary tightening through higher rates aims to align money growth with sustainable output.
Central banks may raise policy rates when inflation persistently exceeds target.
tactical_explanations:
Costlier credit discourages borrowing for consumption and investment. Weaker spending cools the demand that was bidding prices up, so inflationary pressure eases.

So the statement is True.

Higher deposit and bond returns make saving more attractive relative to spending now. Households and firms often postpone purchases, shifting demand toward later periods.

So the statement is True.

Mortgages and equipment loans become more expensive when policy rates rise. That higher financing cost is one channel through which rate increases restrain spending.

So the statement is True.

Tightening seeks to slow nominal spending growth so money and credit do not outrun what the economy can produce sustainably. Aligning money growth with real capacity is the stabilising aim.

So the statement is True.

When inflation stays above target for a sustained stretch, central banks often raise policy rates to cool demand. That response is standard monetary practice against persistent overshoots.

So the statement is True.

title: Tightening Monetary Policy
context: Review how central banks tighten policy by raising interest rates to combat inflation. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher mortgage rates following policy tightening can reduce quantity demanded for new housing loans.
Central banks face a trade-off timing challenge because rate effects appear with lags.
Tightening monetary policy typically involves raising key interest rates or reducing money growth.
Business investment accelerates when higher rates raise the cost of financed equipment purchases.
Policy tightening can never reduce inflation because spending is fixed.
tactical_explanations:
Tighter policy lifts mortgage rates. At higher borrowing costs, fewer households take new housing loans, so quantity demanded for those loans falls.

So the statement is True.

Rate changes alter spending only after firms and households adjust plans. Because those effects arrive with lags, central banks must weigh timing carefully when they tighten.

So the statement is True.

Tightening means making monetary conditions stricter. Raising key policy rates or slowing money growth are the usual tools for that stance.

So the statement is True.

Higher financing costs make equipment loans more expensive, which typically discourages investment. Investment slows rather than accelerates when rates rise.

So the statement is False.

Spending is not fixed with respect to interest rates. Tightening can cool demand over time and thereby reduce inflationary pressure.

So the statement is False.

title: Vienna Mortgage Rate Shopping
context: Consider a Vienna household postponing a flat purchase after the central bank raises mortgage reference rates. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Higher saving returns after rate rises may shift some spending from consumption to deposits.
Postponing a flat purchase reduces current quantity demanded for housing credit.
Central bank rate rises aim to accelerate spending that contributes to inflation.
If many households delay purchases, equilibrium home prices rise because fewer buyers compete.
Higher mortgage reference rates reduce monthly borrowing costs for a given loan amount.
tactical_explanations:
When deposit rates rise with policy rates, saving earns more relative to spending today. Some household funds move into deposits instead of immediate consumption.

So the statement is True.

Delaying the flat purchase means the household does not take a mortgage now. Current quantity demanded for housing credit therefore falls.

So the statement is True.

Rate rises are used to cool spending that feeds inflation, not to accelerate it. The policy aim is restraint, not a spending boom.

So the statement is False.

Fewer competing buyers weaken demand for homes. Weaker demand typically eases upward pressure on equilibrium prices; it does not push prices higher.

So the statement is False.

A higher reference rate raises the interest charged on a given loan size. Monthly borrowing costs rise, they do not fall.

So the statement is False.

title: Demand Increase at Equilibrium
context: Analyze how a rightward demand shift raises equilibrium price and quantity when supply is upward sloping. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Graphically, a demand shift right moves equilibrium up along an upward-sloping supply curve.
Producers respond to higher equilibrium price by reducing quantity supplied along the supply curve.
More buyers entering a market moves buyers along the demand curve without shifting it.
A rightward demand shift with unchanged supply lowers both equilibrium price and quantity.
After demand increases, quantity demanded stays below quantity supplied permanently.
tactical_explanations:
With supply fixed and upward sloping, a rightward demand shift creates a new intersection higher and farther right on the supply curve. Equilibrium price and quantity both rise along that supply path.

So the statement is True.

A higher equilibrium price makes extra units profitable. Along the supply curve, quantity supplied rises with price; producers do not cut quantity when price rises.

So the statement is False.

More buyers at each price is a demand shifter: the whole demand curve moves right. Movement along the curve is caused by a change in the good's own price, not by entry of new buyers.

So the statement is False.

Stronger demand with unchanged supply raises both equilibrium price and quantity. The claim that both fall reverses the standard comparative-static result.

So the statement is False.

After the shift, price adjusts until quantity demanded again equals quantity supplied at the new equilibrium. The imbalance is temporary, not permanent excess supply.

So the statement is False.

title: Supply Decrease at Equilibrium
context: Review how a leftward supply shift raises equilibrium price and lowers equilibrium quantity. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: At the new equilibrium after supply falls, quantity demanded equals the reduced quantity supplied.
Buyers facing higher prices reduce quantity demanded along the demand curve after supply falls.
A leftward supply shift with unchanged demand typically raises equilibrium price and lowers quantity.
Production disruptions can shift supply leftward even when buyer preferences stay constant.
Graphically, a supply shift left moves equilibrium up along a downward-sloping demand curve.
tactical_explanations:
Equilibrium always equates quantity demanded and quantity supplied. After supply falls, that common quantity is simply lower, cleared at a higher price.

So the statement is True.

The leftward supply shift raises the clearing price. Along a downward-sloping demand curve, buyers then take a smaller quantity at that higher price.

So the statement is True.

Less supply at each price, with demand unchanged, pushes the intersection up and left. Equilibrium price rises and equilibrium quantity falls.

So the statement is True.

Disruptions cut what sellers can offer at each price. That is a supply shift even if tastes and other demand factors stay fixed.

So the statement is True.

With demand fixed and downward sloping, a leftward supply shift creates a new intersection higher on the demand curve. Price rises and quantity falls along that demand path.

So the statement is True.

title: Population Growth and Market Demand
context: Analyze how population changes shift market demand for goods and services. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Markets adjust through price when population growth increases quantity demanded at old prices.
Population growth in a city can shift demand rightward for public transport services.
Immigration increasing local consumers can raise equilibrium apartment rents if housing supply is slow.
Demographic changes move buyers along the demand curve without shifting it.
A shrinking town population shifts demand rightward because remaining residents spend more.
tactical_explanations:
More people raise quantity demanded at the old price, creating excess demand. Price then rises toward a new equilibrium that clears the larger demand.

So the statement is True.

Extra residents want more rides at each fare. That non-price change shifts the demand curve for public transport to the right.

So the statement is True.

More local renters shift housing demand right. If supply responds slowly, the new intersection has a higher equilibrium rent.

So the statement is True.

Population is a non-price determinant of demand. Demographic change shifts the demand curve; movement along the curve comes from a change in the good's own price.

So the statement is False.

Fewer residents typically mean less demand at each price, a leftward shift. A shrinking town does not automatically shift demand right just because some people remain.

So the statement is False.

title: Taxes on Producers and Supply
context: Review how taxes levied on sellers can shift supply leftward. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A per-unit tax on producers raises effective production cost and can shift supply leftward.
The statutory incidence on producers can reduce market quantity below the prior equilibrium.
After a producer tax, sellers require lower prices to supply the same quantity as before.
Equilibrium price paid by buyers falls when producer taxes reduce quantity supplied.
Producer taxes move sellers along the supply curve without shifting it.
tactical_explanations:
A per-unit tax adds to the cost of each unit sold. At any given market price, sellers keep less after tax, so they offer less. That is a leftward supply shift.

So the statement is True.

A leftward supply shift with demand unchanged lowers the equilibrium quantity traded. Legal liability on producers therefore can shrink market volume below the old equilibrium.

So the statement is True.

Higher after-tax costs mean sellers need a higher market price to cover the same quantity as before, not a lower one. The claim reverses the cost logic.

So the statement is False.

Less supply with stable demand typically raises the price buyers pay. Buyer price does not fall when producer taxes cut quantity supplied.

So the statement is False.

A cost-changing tax shifts the supply curve. Movement along supply comes from a change in the good's own price, not from the tax itself.

So the statement is False.

title: Subsidies to Producers and Supply
context: Analyze how payments to producers can shift supply rightward. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Subsidised farmers may supply more output at each market price after receiving per-unit payments.
Rightward supply shifts from subsidies raise equilibrium price if demand stays unchanged.
Subsidies differ from price ceilings because both cap buyer prices identically.
Taxpayer-funded subsidies reduce quantity supplied at each price by confusing producers.
Production subsidies lowering effective costs shift demand leftward for the subsidised good.
tactical_explanations:
A per-unit subsidy lowers the net cost of producing each unit. At any given market price, farmers keep more, so they are willing to supply more output. That is a rightward supply shift.

So the statement is True.

More supply with demand unchanged typically lowers the equilibrium price and raises quantity. Subsidies do not raise equilibrium price through a rightward supply shift alone.

So the statement is False.

A subsidy is a payment that changes producers' net costs. A price ceiling is a legal maximum on the price buyers may pay. They are different tools and do not both cap buyer prices identically.

So the statement is False.

Better margins from subsidies encourage more output at each price, expanding supply. They do not cut quantity supplied by confusing producers.

So the statement is False.

Production subsidies act on sellers' costs and shift supply. They do not shift buyer demand left for the subsidised good.

So the statement is False.

title: Weather Shocks and Agricultural Supply
context: Review how adverse weather can shift agricultural supply leftward. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Drought reducing crop yields shifts supply leftward for affected harvests at each price.
Importers may partially offset domestic supply shifts by increasing quantity supplied from abroad.
Short-run food markets may show sharp price spikes after sudden supply leftward shifts.
Frost damaging orchards can raise equilibrium fruit prices if demand remains largely unchanged.
Weather shocks are demand-side events identical to changes in consumer tastes.
tactical_explanations:
Drought cuts yields, so less of the crop is available at each price. That reduction in seller offerings is a leftward supply shift for the affected harvest.

So the statement is True.

Imports add another source of the good. Extra foreign shipments can raise total quantity supplied at each price and partially offset a domestic leftward shift.

So the statement is True.

When supply drops suddenly and demand cannot adjust at once, the clearing price jumps. Short-run food markets often show sharp spikes after such leftward supply shocks.

So the statement is True.

Frost that damages orchards cuts fruit supply. With demand largely unchanged, the new equilibrium has a higher fruit price.

So the statement is True.

Weather changes what producers can harvest; it is a supply-side shock. Changes in tastes are demand shifters. The two are not the same.

So the statement is False.

title: Consumer Expectations and Demand
context: Analyze how expectations about future prices or income shift current demand. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: If buyers expect prices to fall next month, current quantity demanded may decrease today.
Expectations of higher future petrol prices can shift current demand rightward as drivers stock up.
Expected future income growth may shift current demand rightward for durable goods like appliances.
Expectations about future conditions move buyers along the demand curve only.
Panic buying before announced rationing reflects a leftward demand shift at unchanged official prices.
tactical_explanations:
If buyers expect a lower price soon, waiting looks better than buying now. Current quantity demanded can therefore fall even before today's price changes.

So the statement is True.

Expecting higher petrol prices later encourages filling tanks and cans today. At today's price, quantity demanded rises, which is a rightward shift of current demand.

So the statement is True.

Anticipated higher income raises willingness to commit to durables now. Demand for appliances and similar goods can shift right before the income actually arrives.

So the statement is True.

Expectations are a non-price demand shifter. They move the whole demand curve; movement along the curve comes from a change in the good's own price.

So the statement is False.

Panic buying means more purchases at the current official price, a rightward demand shift. It is not a leftward shift that would cut demand.

So the statement is False.

title: Labour Market Wage Adjustment
context: Review how wages coordinate quantity supplied and demanded of labour like prices in goods markets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Labour market equilibrium occurs where quantity supplied of labour equals quantity demanded.
Competition among employers for scarce workers can bid wages up toward labour market equilibrium.
Higher wages typically reduce quantity supplied of labour as workers reject paid work.
Skill shortages in tech hiring resemble goods surpluses with downward wage pressure.
Employers hire more workers when wages rise above the value of marginal output at the margin.
tactical_explanations:
As in goods markets, labour market equilibrium is the wage at which the quantity of labour workers offer equals the quantity employers want to hire.

So the statement is True.

When workers are scarce relative to hiring needs, employers compete for them. That bidding raises wages toward the level that clears the labour market.

So the statement is True.

Higher wages usually draw more people into work or extra hours along the labour supply curve. Quantity supplied of labour typically rises, not falls, when wages rise, other things equal.

So the statement is False.

A skill shortage is excess demand for labour, like a goods shortage. It creates upward wage pressure, not a surplus with downward pressure.

So the statement is False.

Firms hire up to where the wage matches the value of marginal product. If the wage rises above that marginal value, hiring becomes less profitable and quantity demanded falls, not rises.

So the statement is False.

title: Global Supply Chain Disruption
context: Analyze how international supply disruptions shift domestic market supply. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Domestic equilibrium price may rise when import supply falls while demand stays constant.
Global markets isolate domestic equilibrium from supply shocks abroad completely.
Firms may seek alternate suppliers over time, shifting demand leftward permanently.
Port closures delaying imports shift demand rightward for components used in domestic assembly.
Shortages of imported parts increase quantity supplied of finished goods domestically.
tactical_explanations:
Fewer imports cut total domestic supply at each price. With demand unchanged, the new equilibrium typically has a higher price.

So the statement is True.

Trade links domestic markets to foreign supply. Shocks abroad can raise domestic prices and cut quantities; global markets do not fully isolate domestic equilibrium.

So the statement is False.
