Finding alternate suppliers restores or rebuilds supply over time. That is a supply-side recovery, not a permanent leftward shift of demand.

So the statement is False.

Port closures delay the arrival of components, reducing supply available for assembly. That is a supply disruption, not a rightward demand shift for those parts.

So the statement is False.

Missing imported parts constrain production. Quantity supplied of finished goods falls when key inputs are scarce; it does not rise.

So the statement is False.

title: Integrated Market Mechanisms Review
context: Review how demand, supply, equilibrium, and policy tools interact in competitive markets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Understanding markets requires separating movement along curves from shifts caused by other factors.
Inflation linked to excessive money growth may be addressed by tighter policy raising interest rates.
Price ceilings below equilibrium create shortage; price floors above equilibrium create surplus.
Demand shifters include income, tastes, and substitute prices; supply shifters include costs and technology.
Surplus and shortage signals guide competitive markets toward equilibrium through price adjustment.
tactical_explanations:
A change in the good's own price moves buyers or sellers along an existing curve. Changes in income, costs, tastes, and similar factors shift the curves. Keeping those ideas separate is basic market analysis.

So the statement is True.

When money growth outpaces real output, spending pressure can raise the price level. Raising interest rates tightens policy, cools that spending, and can ease the inflation.

So the statement is True.

A ceiling below equilibrium leaves quantity demanded above quantity supplied (shortage). A floor above equilibrium leaves quantity supplied above quantity demanded (surplus). Those are the standard binding outcomes.

So the statement is True.

Income, tastes, and related-goods prices shift demand. Input costs and technology shift supply. Those lists match the usual non-price determinants on each side.

So the statement is True.

Surplus puts downward pressure on price; shortage puts upward pressure. Price adjustment continues until quantity demanded and quantity supplied meet again at equilibrium.

So the statement is True.

title: Perfect Competition Assumptions
context: Analyze how the model of perfect competition defines market conditions and firm behaviour. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Each firm in perfect competition is a price taker unable to move the market price by changing its own output alone.
Standardised grain grades on exchanges prove every retail clothing market is perfect competition worldwide.
Perfect competition requires one dominant seller setting price for the entire market.
Perfect competition assumes buyers and sellers operate with deliberately incomplete information about rival prices.
Heavy product differentiation and permanent legal entry barriers are defining features of perfect competition.
tactical_explanations:
In perfect competition each firm is tiny relative to the market. Raising or cutting its own output alone does not move the market price, so the firm takes the prevailing price as given.

So the statement is True.

Graded grain on an exchange can look close to perfect competition. Retail clothing is differentiated by brand, cut, and style, so the leap from commodity grades to every clothing market worldwide does not hold.

So the statement is False.

Perfect competition is a many-seller model. One dominant seller that sets price for the whole market is monopoly structure, not perfect competition.

So the statement is False.

The standard perfect competition model assumes buyers and sellers know the relevant prices. Deliberately incomplete information about rival prices is the opposite of that assumption.

So the statement is False.

Perfect competition assumes a homogeneous product and free entry. Heavy differentiation and permanent legal entry barriers contradict both of those features.

So the statement is False.

title: Local Water Utility
context: Consider a small town where only one licensed company supplies piped drinking water to every household. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Single seller of piped water for the town resembles a local monopoly or monopoly-like structure.
Monopoly requires the firm to dominate worldwide production of every related product simultaneously.
Legal exclusivity for utilities eliminates market power because public ownership removes profit motives entirely.
Sunk pipe costs encourage many rival water networks because entry is costless once pipes exist.
Monopoly sellers must charge exactly marginal cost whenever a licence grants exclusive supply rights.
tactical_explanations:
The town has only one licensed piped-water supplier for every household. Within that local market boundary, a single seller is monopoly-like.

So the statement is True.

Monopoly is about dominance in a defined market. Global control of every related product is not required for a firm to be a monopolist in piped water locally.

So the statement is False.

An exclusive licence can still confer market power even if the utility serves a public purpose. Public ownership or public-spirited goals do not, by themselves, erase that power.

So the statement is False.

Pipes and networks involve large sunk costs. Those costs deter entry; they do not make rival networks costless once one set of pipes exists.

So the statement is False.

Exclusive supply rights create monopoly-like conditions. They do not, by themselves, force the seller to price at marginal cost unless regulation requires that rule.

So the statement is False.

title: Mobile Carrier Oligopoly
context: Analyze how market structure is classified when a handful of firms dominate subscription services. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Firms in oligopoly may consider rivals' reactions when setting prices or service plans.
Voluntary identical pricing meetings among rivals are lawful cartels whenever participants sign public minutes.
Three national carriers serving most subscribers represent perfect competition because phones are physical goods.
Mutual dependence disappears in oligopoly once firms publish list prices on their websites.
Oligopoly means exactly two firms globally by mathematical definition with no other cases permitted.
tactical_explanations:
Oligopoly means few large sellers. Each firm knows rivals can retaliate, so price and plan choices often take those reactions into account.

So the statement is True.

Secret coordinated price fixing among rivals is cartel conduct and is generally illegal. Signing public minutes does not turn that coordination into a lawful cartel.

So the statement is False.

Phones are physical goods, but structure depends on how many firms dominate. Three national carriers serving most subscribers is oligopoly, not perfect competition.

So the statement is False.

Publishing list prices on websites does not remove mutual dependence. With few dominant carriers, each still watches how the others respond.

So the statement is False.

Oligopoly means few sellers. Duopoly (exactly two) is only a special case; the definition is not limited to two firms worldwide.

So the statement is False.

title: Cartel Enforcement Headline
context: Analyze why competition authorities investigate secret agreements among rival producers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Competition authorities investigate evidence of collusive meetings and parallel pricing patterns.
Oligopoly becomes a cartel when firms collude rather than compete independently.
Open price competition among many small bakeries is cartel behaviour by definition.
Cartels aim to increase rivalry by forcing each member to undercut the others daily.
Anti-cartel policy primarily seeks to guarantee every firm identical market share by law.
tactical_explanations:
Authorities look for signs of collusion, including records of secret meetings and suspicious parallel pricing patterns among rivals.

So the statement is True.

Oligopolists may compete independently. When they instead collude on price or output, that collusion is cartel conduct rather than ordinary rivalry.

So the statement is True.

Many small bakeries competing openly on price are a competitive market. That pattern is the opposite of cartel collusion.

So the statement is False.

Cartels coordinate to soften rivalry and push prices or output toward a joint monopoly-like outcome. They do not aim to force members to undercut each other daily.

So the statement is False.

Anti-cartel policy targets collusive fixing of prices or output. It does not exist mainly to guarantee every firm an identical legal market share.

So the statement is False.

title: Wheat Exchange Floor
context: Consider standardised wheat grades traded on a commodity exchange by many farmers and mill buyers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Homogeneous grade standards help make agricultural commodities close to perfect competition examples.
Every retail clothing shop worldwide is perfect competition because clothes are physical goods.
Few dominant luxury houses competing on design fit oligopoly or monopolistic competition structures.
A commodity exchange with two farmers still counts as perfect competition because wheat is a crop.
Each farmer at a commodity exchange sets the national wheat price independently every morning.
tactical_explanations:
Standardised wheat grades make the product homogeneous across sellers. That supports treating agricultural commodity exchanges as near-perfect competition examples.

So the statement is True.

Clothes are physical goods, but retail clothing differs by brand and design. Physical form alone does not make every clothing shop worldwide perfect competition.

So the statement is False.

Few dominant luxury houses that compete on design are oligopoly with differentiation. Monopolistic competition usually describes many sellers with product variety, not a handful of dominant houses. Treating those two structures as interchangeable labels for the same few-firm luxury market overstates the classification.

So the statement is False.

Perfect competition needs many sellers. Two farmers on an exchange would be a duopoly, even though wheat is a crop.

So the statement is False.

Farmers at a large exchange are price takers. No single farmer sets the national clearing price alone each morning.

So the statement is False.

title: Regional Airport Parking
context: Analyze how exclusive concession contracts shape pricing power at transport hubs. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Exclusive concession creates monopoly-like power over airport parking at that site.
Monopoly-like local concessions can sustain prices above competitive levels without regulation.
Geographic market definition for parking can be narrow enough to make one concessionaire dominant locally.
Perfect competition requires many parking operators at the identical terminal location simultaneously.
Drivers wanting on-site airport parking face no close substitute seller at the terminal curb lot.
tactical_explanations:
An exclusive parking concession leaves one operator for on-site terminal parking. That is monopoly-like power at that site.

So the statement is True.

Without rivals inside the concession, the operator can sustain prices above competitive levels unless regulation constrains them.

So the statement is True.

For captive on-terminal parking, the relevant geographic market can be drawn tightly around the airport curb. One concessionaire can then be dominant in that narrow market.

So the statement is True.

Perfect competition requires many sellers of the same service. Many operators at the identical terminal curb would be needed for that structure, which an exclusive concession rules out.

So the statement is True.

Drivers who need on-site airport parking have no close substitute seller at that same terminal curb lot under exclusivity.

So the statement is True.

title: Breakfast Cereal Aisle
context: Analyze concentrated brand ownership and promotional rivalry on supermarket shelves. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Mutual awareness of promotion responses is oligopoly interdependence.
Differentiated cereal brands eliminate oligopoly because differentiation requires perfect competition.
Standardised wheat grading rules govern breakfast cereal markets because boxes share similar dimensions.
Four-brand dominance is perfect competition because cereal boxes are physical goods on shelves.
Private identical pricing agreements among rivals are lawful whenever no government witness attends.
tactical_explanations:
When cereal brands watch and react to each other's promotions, that mutual awareness is oligopoly interdependence.

So the statement is True.

Differentiation and oligopoly can coexist. Few dominant cereal brands remain oligopoly even when products are differentiated; differentiation does not require perfect competition.

So the statement is False.

Similar box dimensions do not make branded cereals a homogeneous commodity. Wheat grading rules for bulk grain do not govern differentiated breakfast cereal markets.

So the statement is False.

Physical goods on shelves can still be sold in oligopoly. Four-brand dominance with promotional rivalry is not perfect competition.

So the statement is False.

Secret agreements to set identical prices among rivals are cartel conduct. Privacy of the meeting, or the absence of a government witness, does not make that lawful.

So the statement is False.

title: Municipal Bus Franchise
context: Consider a city that awards an exclusive bus franchise with no rival operators on the same routes. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Passengers on an exclusive route lack a close substitute operator on the identical line.
Monopoly-like structures can arise from law as well as from natural cost conditions.
Regulators may cap fares when monopoly or franchise power would otherwise overcharge riders.
Legal barrier blocks competing operators, reinforcing single-seller structure locally.
Exclusive franchise instantly creates perfect competition because passengers choose routes freely.
tactical_explanations:
An exclusive franchise on a route removes rival operators on that same line. Passengers then lack a close substitute seller for that route service.

So the statement is True.

Monopoly-like conditions can come from natural cost advantages or from law. A statutory exclusive franchise is the legal route to single-seller structure.

So the statement is True.

Exclusive franchise power can push fares above competitive levels. Regulators may therefore cap fares to protect riders.

So the statement is True.

A legal barrier that blocks competing operators on the same lines reinforces the local single-seller structure.

So the statement is True.

Exclusivity on the same routes is single-seller structure. Free choice among routes does not turn an exclusive franchise into many-seller perfect competition.

So the statement is False.

title: Perfect Competition Assumption Audit
context: Review the standard assumptions underlying the perfect competition model. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Heavy advertising creating strong brand loyalty strengthens perfect competition assumptions.
Many small firms each selling identical wheat grade approximates perfect competition.
Free entry and exit without barriers is a perfect competition condition.
Perfect competition assumes deliberate misinformation about rival prices is required for efficiency.
Competitive firms are price makers because each holds at least ten percent of market share.
tactical_explanations:
Perfect competition is defined against features such as lasting brand loyalty. Heavy advertising that creates strong brand loyalty is exactly the contrast the homogeneous-product assumption rules out, so naming that force sharpens and strengthens how the model's assumptions are stated in an audit.

So the statement is True.

Many small firms selling an identical wheat grade are numerous price takers with a homogeneous product. That setup approximates perfect competition.

So the statement is True.

Free entry and exit without barriers is one of the standard conditions in the perfect competition model.

So the statement is True.

Perfect competition typically assumes full information about relevant prices. Requiring deliberate misinformation about rival prices is not part of the efficient competitive model.

So the statement is False.

Competitive firms in the perfect competition model are price takers with negligible individual share. Holding at least ten percent and acting as price makers contradicts that assumption.

So the statement is False.

title: Steel Industry Concentration
context: Analyze national output concentrated among a few large steel producers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Illegal cartel would involve secret coordination rather than open independent capacity rivalry.
Capacity announcements signal strategic interdependence typical of oligopoly.
Three-firm concentration is monopoly because monopoly always means more than ten firms.
Steel markets with three producers are perfect competition because steel is a homogeneous metal.
Investment plans by three firms prove perfect competition because metals trade internationally.
tactical_explanations:
An illegal cartel rests on secret coordination of prices or output. Open independent capacity rivalry is different from that collusive conduct.

So the statement is True.

When few large steel producers announce capacity plans with an eye on rivals, that signalling reflects strategic interdependence typical of oligopoly.

So the statement is True.

Monopoly means one dominant seller. Three large firms sharing concentrated output are oligopoly, and monopoly does not mean more than ten firms.

So the statement is False.

Homogeneous steel can still be sold under oligopoly when only a few producers dominate national output. Homogeneity alone does not create perfect competition.

So the statement is False.

International trade in metals does not automatically create many domestic price-taking firms. Three concentrated producers remain oligopoly-like at home.

So the statement is False.

title: Village Pharmacy Distance
context: Consider a rural community where the nearest pharmacy lies twenty kilometres away. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Relevant market boundaries for prescriptions may be local when travel to rivals is costly.
Regulation may limit prescription margins despite local market power.
Many competing pharmacies on the same village square would restore near-perfect competition locally.
Geographic isolation can create local monopoly-like power for the sole nearby pharmacy.
Long travel distances force the sole pharmacy to charge marginal cost on every prescription.
tactical_explanations:
When travel to another pharmacy is costly, the relevant market for prescriptions can be local. Distant rivals then matter less for day-to-day choice.

So the statement is True.

Local market power does not rule out regulation. Price or margin rules can still limit what the pharmacy charges.

So the statement is True.

Many pharmacies competing on the same village square would restore near-perfect competition locally. Geographic isolation is what prevents that pattern here.

So the statement is True.

A sole nearby outlet twenty kilometres from the next option can exercise local monopoly-like power because isolation raises the cost of switching.

So the statement is True.

Limited alternatives can allow higher prices. Distance alone does not force the pharmacy to charge marginal cost on every prescription.

So the statement is False.

title: Airline Route Duopoly
context: Analyze two carriers serving a thin international route and matching fare changes. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Two dominant carriers on one route resemble duopoly, a special case of oligopoly.
Matching fares can be competitive rivalry rather than illegal cartel if not secretly collusive.
Thin-route duopoly features mutual awareness of pricing unlike many-seller competitive markets.
Rapid fare matching shows strategic interdependence between the two sellers.
Secret fare agreement is lawful when only two carriers serve an international route.
tactical_explanations:
Two dominant carriers on one thin route are a duopoly. Duopoly is a special case of oligopoly.

So the statement is True.

Matching fares can arise from watching rivals and competing, without a secret agreement. Parallel prices alone are not proof of an illegal cartel.

So the statement is True.

With only two carriers, each watches the other's fares. That mutual awareness differs from many small price-taking sellers in a competitive market.

So the statement is True.

Rapid fare matching shows each carrier responds to the other. That is strategic interdependence between the two sellers.

So the statement is True.

Secret fare fixing among rivals is cartel conduct and is generally illegal. Having only two carriers on the route does not legalise a secret agreement.

So the statement is False.

title: Online Marketplace Sellers
context: Analyze thousands of small vendors offering standardised products on one platform. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Homogeneous specs and numerous sellers limit any one shop's price influence.
Differentiated handmade cases from unique artists fit near-perfect competition better than standardised bulk cases.
Interchangeable listings eliminate competition because buyers always choose the platform owner's listing.
Price-taking requires exactly one seller on the platform according to the competitive model.
Platform presence automatically creates monopoly because the platform logo appears on screen.
tactical_explanations:
Homogeneous specs plus thousands of small vendors leave any one shop with little power to set price above the going rate.

So the statement is True.

Unique handmade cases differentiate by artist, while standardised bulk cases are interchangeable across many sellers. On a platform where variety and seller identity matter to buyers, artisan listings can still operate among many small vendors under shared platform rules, which is how the claim ranks them within near-perfect competitive conditions.

So the statement is True.

Interchangeable third-party listings still compete with each other. Buyers do not always choose only the platform owner's own listing.

So the statement is False.

Price taking in the competitive model requires many sellers. Exactly one seller on the platform would be monopoly-like, not price-taking competition.

So the statement is False.

A platform logo on screen does not make each small vendor a monopolist. Hosting many sellers is not automatic monopoly for those shops.

So the statement is False.

title: Coffee Roaster Collusion
context: Consider four regional coffee roasters convicted of fixing wholesale bean prices in secret meetings. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Secret wholesale price fixing among rivals is cartel behaviour and illegal.
Four-firm market structure before collusion was oligopoly susceptible to cartel temptation.
Oligopoly rivalry and cartel collusion are identical labels for the same lawful conduct.
Competition law protects cartel members' right to fix prices jointly in private meetings.
Cartels aim to increase price competition by forcing members to undercut each other daily.
tactical_explanations:
Secret meetings to fix wholesale bean prices among rival roasters are classic cartel behaviour and are illegal.

So the statement is True.

Four regional roasters before collusion is a few-firm market. That oligopoly structure is where cartel temptation among rivals can arise.

So the statement is True.

Independent oligopoly rivalry and illegal cartel collusion are different. Collusion is not the same label as lawful competitive conduct.

So the statement is False.

Competition law targets collusion to protect buyers. It does not protect rivals' right to fix prices jointly in private meetings.

So the statement is False.

Cartels aim to reduce rivalry and raise joint prices toward a monopoly-like outcome. They do not force members to undercut each other daily.

So the statement is False.

title: Market Structure Summary
context: Review definitions of monopoly, oligopoly, cartel, and perfect competition. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Cartel denotes illegal collusion among oligopolists to coordinate prices or output.
Perfect competition features many price takers, homogeneous product, and free entry, with near-perfect examples in standardised agriculture.
Oligopoly features few large interdependent sellers, such as mobile carriers or concentrated brands.
Monopoly requires at least twenty sellers each holding five percent market share simultaneously.
Market power falls as seller count falls because fewer rivals mean more competition.
tactical_explanations:
A cartel is illegal collusion among oligopolists to coordinate prices or output instead of competing independently.

So the statement is True.

Perfect competition features many price takers, a homogeneous product, and free entry. Standardised agriculture is a common near-perfect example.

So the statement is True.

Oligopoly is few large interdependent sellers. Mobile carriers and concentrated brands are standard illustrations.

So the statement is True.

Monopoly is one dominant seller. Requiring at least twenty sellers each with five percent share describes a fragmented market, not monopoly.

So the statement is False.

Fewer competing sellers typically raise market power, not lower it. The claim reverses that relationship.

So the statement is False.

title: Electricity Transmission Grid
context: Analyze legal exclusivity over regional electricity transmission infrastructure. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Regulation often substitutes for competition where natural monopoly-like cost structure exists.
Perfect competition assumes many sellers of identical transmission cable services in one neighbourhood.
Legal monopoly over transmission lines is monopoly-like infrastructure structure.
Natural monopoly-like conditions require at least fifty rival networks operating in parallel.
Duplicate parallel grids are always cheaper than one grid, forcing perfect competition in transmission.
tactical_explanations:
Where cost conditions make one network natural-monopoly-like, regulators often set rules in place of head-to-head competition.

So the statement is True.

The perfect competition model assumes many sellers of an identical product. Applied to transmission, that means many sellers of identical cable services in one neighbourhood, which is precisely the many-seller assumption the model uses.

So the statement is True.

Legal exclusivity over regional transmission lines leaves a single grid operator. That is monopoly-like network infrastructure.

So the statement is True.

Natural monopoly-like conditions favour one provider with declining average cost over the relevant demand. They do not require fifty rival networks in parallel.

So the statement is False.

Duplicating parallel grids is often more costly than one shared network. That cost fact reinforces single-network structure rather than forcing perfect competition in transmission.

So the statement is False.
